The optional WebGL2 backend detaches a VAO element buffer before binding a different one. Raw GL replay on ANGLE D3D11 reproduced retired reference indices in a correctly bound replacement, with zero GL errors; detaching repairs exact bytes without a GPU wait. The CPU replay regression checks changed and unchanged bindings; the canonical material wireframe gate adds repeated transparent/mirrored replacements at 1x and 4x and passes 285 checks on each backend. Dispersion remains unproven despite two passing full compat runs. See docs/whitepaper/materials-compat-hunt.md. No core/stage or shader math change.
### Section 5 evidence: batch 163 line work

Lines omits identical frame uploads using exact Uint32 word comparison and invalidates on GPU buffer recreation. Independent butt/square segments omit only endpoint-degenerate fan triangles. CPU tests assert work counts and exact uniform bytes; package GPU tests compare every pixel against forced original work at 1x/4x MSAA. No core, stage or shared implementation change. [Method](../whitepaper/bp-163-workcounts.md#job-3-line-and-skeleton-draw-work).
Batch 159 round 2 corrects EXT/KHR meshopt fallback handling in gltf/pbr, including
the async resolver's download decision. Synthetic compressed triangle accessors
match byte for byte under both names; hostile fallback references and dual names
reject. The previous snapshot inventory remains historical, with current readiness
checked separately. No backend, decoder arithmetic, core, stage or API changed.
[Regression and standards](../whitepaper/parity-diagnoses.md#round-2-meshopt-fallback-parsing).

### 5. Compute distance fields (jump flooding, 2026-11-10)

The optional compute/distance entry adds one WGSL kernel (seed, flood, distance and site-id modes of one shader, 8 x 8
workgroups, integer squared distances, ties to the lower index) with no core, stage or backend change. Evidence: error
rates against the exact separable transform on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer, nearest-seed buffers bit-identical to the CPU
backend, 200 brute-force oracle masks (docs/limits.md, "Compute distance fields"). Missing: quiet-machine GPU timings
(the speed-phase inventory) and the follow-up consumers (coast foam, outline widening).

### 5. Audio offline spectrograms (2026-11-10)

The optional audio/spectrogram entry is CPU code (radix-2 FFT in double precision, two real frames per transform) with a
GPU path that loads compute/fft lazily and batches frames; no core, stage or backend change. Evidence: windows against Harris's
formulas, FFT against a direct DFT, Parseval, round trip within 6e-8, Griffin-Lim SNR and convergence, GPU against CPU on both
backends (docs/limits.md, "Audio offline spectrograms"). Missing: the Rust/Wasm FFT A/B and quiet-machine timings
(the speed-phase inventory), the phase vocoder.

## Section 5 evidence: lague plan 1 particle liquid
Optional water/liquid (ParticleLiquid) is an HDR PostStack stage of six render passes: sphere sprites to r32float eye depth with a depth32float attachment, three narrow-range filter passes (Truong and Yuksel 2018), additive r16float thickness, one composite. It reads particle centres from a storage buffer in the vertex stage (the WebGL2 layer's data texture) and uses no compute, workgroup memory, barriers or 32-bit float blending, so both backends run the same WGSL as draws. Evidence: packages/water/test/liquid.browser.mjs passes natively and with MARGO_COMPAT=1 (GPU filter equals the float64 oracle within 1e-4 at every covered pixel, refraction and Fresnel against ray optics, steady-frame work counts at 1,000,000 particles). Missing: the iGPU timing and the quiet-machine rerun (the speed-phase inventory). No core, stage or water root change.
Whitewater (2026-11-11): a lazy chunk of seven render-pass pipelines (bucket fill by depth-tested point draws into r32uint, normals and potentials into rgba32float and r32uint, a count pyramid in two r32uint atlases, the pool step as MRT into two rgba32float targets, a 1x1 ring head, sprites into an rgba16float layer the composite reads). No compute, atomics, workgroup memory or barriers, so the WebGL2 layer runs every pass as a draw; its fragment stages read storage buffers through the layer's data textures. Evidence: packages/water/test/liquid-whitewater.browser.mjs passes natively and with MARGO_COMPAT=1 with identical counts, equal to the float64 oracle on the first step; the CPU test checks and translates every shader with the layer's own WGSL front end. Missing: iGPU timing and the quiet rerun.

Narrow band (2026-11-11, packages/water/src/liquid-band.ts, Oliveira and Paiva 2022): a lazy chunk of render passes only (bounds reduction, a 1x1 grid pass, additive voxel counts in rgba16float, two r32uint label passes, depth sprites culled in the vertex stage, one thickness ball per voxel), so the WebGL2 layer runs it as draws. Evidence: packages/water/test/liquid-band.browser.mjs, native and MARGO_COMPAT=1, labels equal the Algorithm 1 oracle, nearest depth identical with and without the band. Missing: quiet timing to set the default.

## Sciviz volume march physics and filter precision (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-11)

GPU maths change in `@margoengine/sciviz` volume marches (`volume.ts`, `multivolume.ts`, `bricks.ts`,
`cinematic-shader.ts`, `volume-quality*.ts`): steps in data units against the finest voxel, voxel-centre texel
addressing, model-matrix view direction, density as an extinction scale, full-length preintegration segments, and
multivolume scene-depth clipping (docs/known-bugs.md, "Fixed 2026-11-11: sciviz volume march physics"). Evidence:
`tests/volume-physics-browser.mjs`, the spike case of `tests/volume-quality-browser.mjs`, `tests/volume-depth-browser.mjs`,
both backends. Quality gate change: the one-brick check of `tests/bricks-browser.js` compares whole and bricked under a
test-only exact float trilinear filter (pipeline constant `filterMode`; the normal path builds the hardware branch
only) at 1 of 255, and bounds each hardware march by an 8-bit filter-weight model (measured worst 6 within the model's
8); docs/limits.md, "Sciviz volume filtering precision". Since 2026-11-15 the model's sign is exact integer arithmetic
(pcg3d of the position on the 1/256 sub-texel grid, Jarzynski and Olano 2020) instead of a `sin` hash, whose accuracy
WGSL leaves open outside [-pi, pi], and the bound is the worst of 16 seeded patterns; a check requires the GPU to draw
the CPU's sign at all 262,144 probe positions. Evidence: Apple M6 native and WebGL2 layer identical per pattern (bound
8, hardware 4). Still missing: the same measurement on an AMD or Intel GPU since this change.

Opacity 1 (KB5700a, 2026-11-11): the per-step opacity correction of the scalar, bricked, multi-volume, quality and
curvilinear marches, and of GPU volume picking, takes alpha exactly 1 when the classified opacity is 1 and the step is
positive (opacity 1 is infinite extinction), instead of 1 - 1e-6^k or a 0.999999 clamp. Tetrahedral and AMR marches
already did. The cinematic path tracer keeps its 0.9999 extinction clamp (a finite free-flight distance). Evidence:
case 8 of `tests/volume-physics-browser.mjs`, `opaque` in `tests/curvilinear-browser.mjs`, the opacity check of
`tests/bricks-browser.js` and `tests/pick-gpu-browser.mjs` (threshold 1), both backends on the A6000.

## GPU work per submission on small GPUs (KB-BL1, section 5 supplement, 2026-11-11)

A voxel path tracer suite crashed the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M). The tracer's bound counted paths per dispatch (2^20,
measured on the RTX A6000 at 8 bounces); it ignored the path loop's length, the GPU's speed, and that a viewport frame's
bands shared one submission, which a GPU preempting only between packets runs whole against Windows' 2 s watchdog.
The rule for GPU kernels now: bound work (items x loop iterations) per submission, not per dispatch; start a new device
small and size later submissions from its measured speed; keep any timing-driven split to one that changes no value
(row bands), with value-affecting splits (sample runs) fixed by work counts alone. Evidence: work counts in
`packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/dispatch-budget.test.js`; bit-identical bands in the browser check's `determinism`
case. Still missing: the AMD mini PC validation run under a heat watchdog (recorded in docs/known-bugs.md when done).

KB4037 (2026-11-28) showed the first figure and the smallest piece were still sized for fast GPUs: a Ryzen 9 9950X's
two-unit RDNA2 graphics ran the denoise-materials bands 140 to 600 times slower than the RTX A6000 and reset on the
third. The rule gains three parts: a new device starts at a 128th of the per-submission work; a band whose fewest rows
are still over the budget is cut into column pieces (any split that changes no value may follow timing); and pieces
are made one at a time from the budget measured last, never planned for a whole run in advance. The shortest piece is
then one thread's fixed run of samples, which bounds what timing can do; evidence and the remaining limit are in
docs/known-bugs.md (KB4037).

## Plugin lifetime in check:owners (integration J1, list 5 batch I1, 2026-11-11)

A plugin package proves its lifetime with a `test(s)/owner-lifetime.fixture.js` run by `npm run check:owners`, not by a
runner of its own (manager ruling, 2026-11-11). Write the fixture with the package; a package printed as pending is not
checked. The shared harness (`tests/support/owner-lifetime.js`) runs every entry in the default and a second scene,
through dispose, detach, scene and engine disposal, device loss attached and detached, and `cycles` (three more
attaches and disposals, GPU objects alive must not grow), and fails on a leaked listener, GPU object or `onFrame`
callback, `engine.views` left changed, a pass still running after disposal or a same-name plugin in the other scene
removed. Each new check has a deliberate-defect test in `tests/owner-lifetime.test.js`. An entry that uses a fixed set
a package makes once per device on first use (materials' 1x1 default textures) sets `warmUp` to its reason: the
harness uses that set up once per device before measuring and after a device loss, never a waiver for a leak per
attach. Details and the revert proofs: docs/integration-fixtures.md.

Packages whose public objects are not engine plugins but hold a lifetime (listeners, timers, workers, storage handles,
signal subscriptions) tie the object to a plugin registration with `ownedByEngine` (`tests/support/owner-shell.js`), so
the harness sees the object's own listeners and releases it through the same six lifetimes; `watchTimers` there adds
the timer check the harness lacks, `tests/support/owner-dom.js` gives a panel its document (the page's own in a
browser leaf, jsdom in the CPU leaf, where listeners on jsdom nodes are not observed). Batch owners-b1 (2026-11-15)
gated math, fsm, tween, ecs, save, cache, behavior, input, wfc and splines: eight with fixtures (fsm, tween, ecs,
save, cache, behavior, input, wfc) and two excluded because their source holds nothing with a lifetime (math, splines;
`tests/owner-exclusions.test.js` reads that source and fails if it gains a listener, timer, worker, storage handle, GPU
resource or engine registration). Gated now: 42 packages with fixtures, 6 excluded (core, physics, physics2d, ragdoll
by ruling; math, splines audited), 59 still pending (it was 69 before this batch). Leaks the fixtures found: cache `Prefetcher` left
its abort listener on an app signal after `dispose()`; input `Gyro.dispose()` left a pending `calibrate()` timer and
signal listener; save `indexedDBStorage` had no way to close its database connection (now `close()` and
`using`). Batch owners-b3 (2026-11-15) added fixtures for worker and gltf (its async loads build in the scene they
started in since KB-OWN-GLTF1) and audited and excluded kinematics-constraints (solvers on numbers and typed arrays):
44 packages with fixtures, 7 excluded, 56 pending on its own; with batch owners-b2 and the usdz fixture beside it, 49 with
fixtures, 7 excluded and 51 pending. Batch owners-b7 (2026-11-15) added fixtures for fbx, mixer and rigging: 52
packages with fixtures, 7 excluded, 48 pending. What they found: fbx `loadFBX`, `parseFBXInWorker` and
`loadFBXInWorker` built their model in the scene active when they finished (KB-OWN-FBX1); rigging `addPoseTracking`
and `playVRMA` stayed live when their scene removed their plugin, and their later `dispose()` removed a same-name
plugin (KB-OWN-RIG1). mixer holds Web Audio graphs, which no runtime lets a page list, so its entries run on a recording
context in both leaves and check every edge, started source and worklet port themselves. Batch owners-b9 (2026-11-15)
added fixtures for loaders and exporters: with the batches landed beside it, 58 packages with fixtures, 7
excluded, 42 pending. What it found: rigging
`addFace` and `addVRM` stayed live when their scene removed their plugin (KB-OWN-RIG2); loaders `loadOBJ` kept its
materials and textures after its scene removed the mesh (KB-OWN-LOAD1); and, writing the blender fixture, the .margo
parse and load functions built in the scene active when they finished (KB-OWN-BLEND1; components and lightmap
followed in batch owners-b10 as KB-OWN-BLEND2, with glTF physics attaching and the physics wrapper disposing its world
in the active scene instead of the model's). Batch owners-b10 (2026-11-15) added the blender fixture (7 entries, 91
cases, its components entry runs the real physics world and lights) and the tiles fixture (TilesRenderer with a GLB,
a points and a decorated root tile, and TileFeatures; 52 cases) and the tonemap fixture (8 entries, 104 cases): 61
packages with fixtures, 7 excluded, 39 pending. The tonemap fixture found that a removed Tonemap kept its LocalExposure
textures (KB-OWN-TONE1). Exporters register nothing; their entries check that a call leaves no signal listener, GPU object or
mesh behind. Asynchronous disposal (same batch): a handle whose `dispose` returns a promise, or that has
only `Symbol.asyncDispose`, and a plugin whose `dispose` returns one, are awaited before any release is asserted, each
with a hard limit of 5,000 ms (`DISPOSE_LIMIT_MS` in `tests/support/owner-lifetime.js`); a disposal that never
settles fails the entry by name, one that rejects fails with its own error, and one that settles holding a listener
fails as a leak (`tests/owner-lifetime-async.test.js`). With it ecs `ParallelSchedule` (`stop()` and
`Symbol.asyncDispose`, with a stand-in worker; in the CPU leaf only, since `SharedArrayBuffer` needs a cross-origin
isolated page and the browser owner page is not one) and cache `LoadingManager` (a request aborted in flight, one with
the app's own signal, one read to its end) have fixture entries. Still not covered: the real Worker of ecs
`ParallelSchedule` (`packages/ecs/test/parallel.test.js` covers its termination) and of wfc `WFCWorkerSolve` (a
stand-in worker is used; `packages/wfc/test/worker-host.mjs` runs the real one). Batch owners-b12 (2026-11-15) added the xr fixture (recording `navigator.xr`; XR.create, XR.attach, an inline session and XRModels, 52 cases each leaf), the ifc fixture (78 cases), the cad fixture (52 CPU, 65 browser) and the robot-planning fixture (52), and excluded brep as pure: 69 packages with fixtures, 8 excluded, 30 pending. It found that XRModels built its models in whichever scene was active when a frame arrived (KB-OWN-XR1), that the WebGL2 compatibility device left its context-loss listener on the canvas after destroy (KB-OWN-COMPAT1, a backend fix), that cad's loadCAD, parseCADAsync and PartInstancer built in or stayed in the wrong scene (KB-OWN-CAD1, CAD2) and that the part pack drew outside its view's scissor (KB-OWN-CAD3).

Batch owners-b2 (2026-11-15) gated lines, viewcube, toon and water: 46 packages with fixtures, 6 excluded and 55
pending. Its fixtures found five defects, each fixed with a regression test: Lines and LineBatches `dispose()` left the
plugin and its draw pass registered (packages/lines/tests/dispose-registration.test.js); Water released and retook the
shared scene-depth capture on a device restore, replacing its registration (packages/water/test/restore-depth.test.js);

Batch owners-b6 (2026-11-15) gated tilemap, terrain and scenery: with the batches landed beside it, 56 packages with
fixtures, 7 excluded and 44 pending (107 packages; road follows below). The lightmap fixture landed with KB-OWN-LIGHTMAP1, and the biomes one with KB-OWN-BIOMES3 (its detail and far-forest density maps are made for the device drawing now), which leaves 42 pending. terrain's 25 entries run one leaf per entry (`leafPerEntry`). The CPU model's stand-in core

Batch owners-b8 (2026-11-15) gated road: 59 packages with fixtures, 7 excluded and 41 pending. `roadGraph` returns a

plays the caller: a compute context on the engine's device (the fixture's dependency, ended at cleanup), the graph, a

## Shot look checks (shorts P4, section 5 supplement, 2026-11-14)

`@margoengine/headless/look` is the review gate for rendered shots, not an engine gate: CPU functions over probe frames,
masks and float frames, bounded by each shot file's `lookBounds`, giving a table and a contact sheet. Evidence: each
check fails a synthetic defect and passes a clean frame (packages/headless/tests/look.test.js); run on the Storm Light
tour probes from tools/shot it flagged two light discs (lamp and marker post, both real lights, so the shot's bound
must say 2) and 3 % crushed rock in the opening frame. Missing: the inputs the shot tool does not write yet (float
frame, view-projection, compat and 16-sample reference frames, still-camera runs, foam and dark masks), so those checks
have no evidence on real shots; bounds are not calibrated against viewers. No rendering backend, kernel or tier code
changes.

Empty masks (2026-11-15, KB-HEARTH-CLIP1 part 1): `skyClip`, and `grain` and `lights` given a mask, set `empty` on a
row measured over a mask with no pixels in it and the report prints `pass (measured 0 sky pixels)`, so a shot with no
sky in view never passes silently. Evidence: packages/headless/tests/look.test.js and tests/shot-look.test.js. Missing:
a sky derived by the shot tool for every page. A view target's depth is not the scene's depth on a page with a
PostStack (it draws into its own target), measured on cabin-window-snow: the derived mask read 100 % sky.

Sky coverage (2026-11-15, KB-HEARTH-CLIP1 part 2): `@margoengine/sky`'s opt-in `coverage` option records where the sky
drew into `coverageTexture` (r8unorm, resolved from the frame's samples): its full-screen triangle again, at the same
depth with the same `greater-equal` test against the frame's depth, so it is exact under a PostStack. Off by default
(no pass, no allocation); on, one render pass a frame. No core or stage change (`npm run measure:size` unchanged);
`@margoengine/sky/base` grew from 6,912 to 7,270 B gzip and `@margoengine/headless/look` from 10,814 to 11,036 B. The
shot tool reads it as `sky-coverage` on probe frames when a shot has no `sky` mask, and `skyClip` alone measures
inside it; `grain`, `lights` and `horizonSeam` keep the page's mask, and the 0.5 bound is unchanged. Evidence:
packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs `coverage` (A6000, WebGPU and compat, 4x and 1x MSAA: 0 of 9,360 wall pixels and
9,360 of 9,360 open sky pixels, HDR scene identical with the record on), packages/sky/test/sky.test.js,
packages/headless/tests/look.test.js, tests/shot-look.test.js, tools/shot/test/determinism-check.mjs (case 7) and
tools/shot/test/sky-coverage-check.mjs. Measured on the A6000 at full size: cabin-hearth-kettle `skyClip` over the
whole frame 1.294, 2.159 and 4.779 % (fail), inside the coverage 0 sky pixels (pass); cabin-window-snow sky share
18.1, 15.0 and 11.6 %, `skyClip` 0; orrery-dolly unchanged (no sky). Missing: Mac and laptop runs.

Weather cover slope bias (section 5, 2026-11-14, lane SC6): PrecipitationCover's receiver test adds sqrt(2) texels times the receiver's slope to its bias for surfaces facing up (normal y 0.5 or more), so a sloped shelter no longer shelters its own top in texel-spaced stripes (Williams 1978; Dou et al. 2014, JCGT). Evidence: the slope probes of packages/weather/tests/cover-check.html on the 680M (WebGPU; the cover is WebGPU-only), 24 of 24 exposed with the fix and 3 of 24 without; walls and flat receivers unchanged.

Contrast as a power about grey (section 5, 2026-11-14, lanes SC7 and SC10): Tonemap (display-linear, `margoContrast`) and creative's PostProcessing (scene-linear) apply contrast k as 0.18 (x / 0.18)^k, a slope of k in log2 exposure (ACEScc, Academy S-2014-003; ASC CDL v1.2 power), instead of (x - 0.18) k + 0.18 clamped at 0, which clipped every channel below 0.18 (1 - 1/k) to black and left flat banded runs. Evidence on the 680M: the contrast 1.08 frames of packages/tonemap/tests/curves-browser.mjs (1,456,524 dark channels black before, 0 after) and packages/creative/tests/post-contrast-browser.mjs at 1.2 (695,400 of 698,258 visible dark channels black before, 0 after, 2.43 levels from the power). Missing: A6000 and Mac runs of both. Contrast 0 (lane SC13) is flat 0.18, black included, returned before the power, because pow(0, 0) is undefined in WGSL (exp2(y log2 x)) and GLSL ES 3.00 (8.2); evidence on the 680M, WebGPU and compat: packages/tonemap/tests/contrast-zero-browser.mjs and packages/creative/tests/post-contrast-zero-browser.mjs (every pixel the flat grey; without it 115,920 and 230,400 channels black on WebGPU).

### 5. Batch 228 job 2: point style evidence
The optional points/style entry evaluates attribute filters and OGC 3D Tiles point styles on the CPU and draws through existing GPU paths only: per-point colours and sizes, the selection mask in filter mode (vertex-stage discard, unpickable), a subset PointCloud, or per-node octree data. No shader, pipeline or backend changed. Evidence: packages/points/tests/style.test.js (CPU, real USGS tile included) and styleFilters in packages/points/tests/features-browser.js on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer. The 3D Tiles interpreter moved from tiles into packages/shared/style-expression.js, covered by both packages' style tests.

WebGL2 layer on Apple silicon (section 5, 2026-11-15): Metal under ANGLE and Dawn is one sampler (explicit LOD snapped to 1/64, footprint LOD about 1/256), so the mip blend checks (test/blend-check.mjs) hold the layer to native bit for bit when the raw WebGL2 probe equals native's; the driver-blend comparison stays for a WebGL2 blend that differs (AMD D3D11). The inverse trigonometry probe includes signed-zero atan2 inputs, which Metal gets a half turn wrong, so the layer uses its own acos, asin, atan and atan2 there (docs/known-bugs.md, "Metal mip blend" and "atan2 with x = -0"). Evidence: features-browser.mjs and bias-browser.mjs pass on an Apple M6; native Metal atan2 at x = -0 stays open below Margo.

### Clean-frame look bar (headless/look, 2026-11-17, quality gates)

The look gate gained the clean-frame checks T1 to T8 and the `animatedFeature` look family (a shot file's `lookFamily`).
Evidence: packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js fails each defect on a synthetic frame (hard against resolved edges,
a shifted pattern warped by `reprojectionMotion`, a sharp against a smeared mover, outline contrast, shape, bounce and
b*). Missing: probes at supersample 2 with 8 sub-frames, which the roadmap bounds assume.

**Real masks (KB-LOOK-SHADOWMASK1, 2026-11-17).** `SceneTargets` (`@margoengine/post/mrt`) gains the sun's shadow
visibility as `t.shadow`: in the core replay the term a shadow plugin wrapped around `direct` in `let linear=` is kept
live with `direct` set to 1 (Rec. 709 luminance of a coloured result); gltf/pbr, materials and terrain captures call
`shadowLit(vec3f(1), position, normal)` when their lit code has it. Built-in `penumbra`, `litGround`, `shadedGround` and
`subject` values draw the look masks; the targets pass moves from order -5 to -4.5, after every -5 shader patch and the
shadow-map render whatever the attach order (before, a SceneTargets attached ahead of Shadows read last frame's maps
and an unpatched shader). The shot tool writes those masks through `aovs`, so T1 penumbra, T5 and T6 run on real
shots. Evidence: post test/scene-targets.test.js (replay text, order, formats, subject and terrain hooks),
test/scene-targets-shadow-browser.mjs (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer: terrain and core floor shadows, visibility 0.0002
shaded against 0.99999 lit, the frame darker inside the shaded mask, 1 everywhere with Shadows removed),
tools/shot/test/look-masks-check.mjs (every mask check runs on a real shot). Missing: local lights' shadows in the
visibility, core meshes as the subject.

**T6 compares within blocks of the frame (KB-LOOK-TV-POOLFAILS1, 2026-11-28).** `bounce` and `shadowTint` compare lit
and shadowed ground only within blocks a tenth of the frame's shorter side (`GROUND_BLOCK`, 108 pixels at 1080p), each
block one more stratum beside the albedo's, so light that changes across the frame does not read as the shadow's (a
shadow read across its own edge: Finlayson, Hordley, Lu and Drew 2006; slow illumination: Land and McCann 1971); bounds
unchanged. Evidence: the rail-line's sun is 1.6 percent of its ground's light and its 74 shadowed pixels a frame sit
beside the fire wall, whose glow lights the haze; T6 read 137.7 / 139.3 percent and -4.7 / -4.8 b* across the frame and
94.8 / 95.3 percent and +0.64 / +0.58 b* within blocks (98 predicted). Aftermath, fire-line and town-street still pass
(88 to 96 percent becomes 95 to 96); valley-aerial goes from 20.4 to 101.0 percent, still failing, its own cause open.
Regression: headless tests/look-clean.test.js (a glow across the frame; 145 percent without blocks).

**T6 compares like surfaces (KB-LOOK-TV-TINTMATCH1, 2026-11-28).** With an albedo (`albedo-r`, `albedo-g`, `albedo-b`
masks, `albedoOf`) `bounce` and `shadowTint` compare lit and shadowed ground within strata of like albedo (16 levels per
sRGB channel), pooled with Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weights; bounds unchanged. Evidence: headless tests/look-clean.test.js
(two surfaces under one light); the blowup's mid T6 went from 103.6 percent and 0.036 b* (different surfaces) to 103.7
and -0.55 over 128 matched pixels. Missing: a resolution rule, since the blowup's difference has a standard error of
0.14 b* against a 0.0448 floor (KB-LOOK-TV-TINTRES1).

**T6 reads the masks' interiors (KB-LOOK-TV-BOUNCE1, 2026-11-26).** The masks are a sharp capture; the frame is resolved
from supersamples with motion blur, depth of field and bloom, so a pixel on a mask's edge holds both sides. `bounce` and
`shadowTint` (`@margoengine/headless/look`) average each ground mask's interior, `GROUND_INSET` (1/360 of the frame's
shorter side, 3 pixels at 1080p) in from every edge; bounds unchanged. Evidence: the calm rail-line shot read bounce 146.5
percent with the edges and 15.0 without (the lights give 19 on level soil); headless tests/look-clean.test.js holds
blurred 9-pixel shadow strips to their sharp value. Missing: the same inset for `grain` in the penumbra band, whose
one-pixel interior may be too thin at 1080p (KB-LOOK-TV-PENUMBRA2).

**Plants in the masks (KB-LOOK-MASKOCCLUDE1, 2026-11-26).** A lit `Scatter` (`@margoengine/scatter`, the `material`
option) is a capture model: `setCapture`/`draw(c, 'capture')` draw this frame's three LOD rings (the main camera's culled
set, as `drawShadow`) into the hook's pass with the colour pass's own lit stage (vertex, wind, LOD dither, blade normal,
maps and cut-out), its lighting kept in a dead block and the return replaced by the hook's `margoSSR` (scatter
`src/capture.ts`), depth greater-equal and written. Capture pipelines are keyed by the effect's declarations and kept
apart from the colour pipelines, so one Scatter in two effects never recompiles either. `SceneTargets.add(model,
{ground: false})` sets `t.ground` 0, so `litGround` and `shadedGround` read 0 on plants while they still hide the ground
and write every other output; core's Frame text (`struct Frame { camera`) is accepted by the terrain-form hook.
`BiomeObjects` and `BiomeView` forward one hook to every child scatter (and the view to its terrain and horizon).
Evidence: scatter test/capture.test.js (stage text, hook checks, per-effect cache, textured cut-out),
post test/scene-targets.test.js, biomes tests/objects.test.js (shared hook, release, disposed parts),
post test/scene-targets-scatter-browser.mjs (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer: 466 lit and 341 shaded ground pixels on the
plants before, 0 and 0 with `{ground: false}`, 823 plant pixels, mean height 0.63 m, 52 edge pixels apart from the
4x multisampled frame). Missing: `ScatterInstances` capture, the timber-valley masks check on a real shot, and the
cost on a forest (one draw per ring per scatter per effect). A ring replaced by `ScatterTiles` growing (`instancesChanged()`) drops the capture ring groups with the colour ones, and the WebGL2 route arriving drops the capture stages, so a capture never binds a destroyed ring (KB-SCATTER-CAPTURESTALE1; scatter `test/capture.test.js`).

**Water in every capture effect (KB-WATER-TARGETS1, KB-WATER-STALEDEPTH1, 2026-11-26).** Water writes SSR's three
fields only for SSR's own `MargoSSR` and otherwise returns the hook's `margoSSR` with its surface, so SceneTargets,
MeshBlend and LightBounce take it; SceneTargets and MeshBlend recognise gltf's `Surface` by its `base` field (water has
its own `Surface`), and SceneTargets reads the sun from a Frame's `light` or water's `sun`. A capture that runs before
the water's own draw rebinds a scene depth that changed since (a replaced post stack). Evidence: water
test/capture.test.js, post test/scene-targets.test.js and test/mesh-blend.test.js, post
test/scene-targets-water-browser.mjs (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer). Missing: water's shadow visibility in `t.shadow`
(it reads 1 on water).

**Sky occlusion (KB-LOOK-POST-SKYOCC1, 2026-11-17, GPU maths).** GTAO's kernel gains `sky()`: with `skyRadius` above 0
(frame `size.zw` = reach and steps, both 0 when off) the slices search their horizons again out to the reach, samples
spaced by the square of their index from 1 pixel out (4 before KB-GTAO-OPENFLOOR1), each sample slid into the slice, and the
visible arc is clamped to the normal's hemisphere and the sky half of the slice (world up projected into it, angle u).
The visible share of the sky arc, by the paper's closed form made signed (`skyArc(h) = sign(h) arc(h)`), over the open
sky arc multiplies the occlusion. Off, the sky term returns 1 before any work and the multiply by 1 is exact: the
occlusion values matched the previous build value for value (81 values on three scenes, RTX A6000). Evidence: post
test/gtao.test.js (uniform, validation, the shader's own arc giving an infinite slot's view factor to 1e-4 over 3600
slices), test/settings.test.js (rows and the animatedFeature value), test/gtao-sky-browser.mjs (WebGPU and the WebGL2
layer: open floor 0.998, slope 0.9998, slot 0.471 against 0.447). Found: the plain GTAO reads 0.980 on an open floor
seen 53 degrees off its normal (samples 1 to 3 pixels out lift its horizon; KB-GTAO-OPENFLOOR1). Missing: timing,
other GPUs.

**GTAO samples slid into their slice (KB-GTAO-OPENFLOOR1, 2026-11-17, GPU maths).** Cause: each horizon sample reads the
pixel nearest its point on the slice's screen line, up to half a pixel off it, so 1 to 3 pixels out its screen direction
turns by up to 45 degrees; a tilted plane's horizon depends on that direction, so an open floor seen 53 degrees off its
normal read 0.980 (a float64 CPU replica of the kernel gives 0.980 too: rounding, not depth precision; exact sub-pixel
positions give 1). Fix: both the GTAO and the sky terms move each sample back into the slice along the surface's tangent
plane, `delta - slide (axis . delta)` with `slide = w / (axis . w)` and `w` the slice axis minus its part along n. The
sample's height above the tangent plane, the quantity that occludes, is kept and a sample already in the slice is
unchanged; projecting along the slice axis changes that height and does not help. The falloff keeps the true distance,
and the sky search now starts 1 pixel out. Evidence (RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer, post
test/gtao-sky-browser.mjs, failing on the old kernel at 0.977): the plain GTAO reads 0.99996 to 1.00004 on the open
floor and slope; a 90 degree crease of floor and wall stays near 0.5 (0.674 after the blur at its darkest pixel, 0.690
before); the wedge proof (`post-effects-gpu.mjs --only=gtao`, record results/gtao-gpu.json) moves 0.525 to 0.520, 0.267
to 0.268, 0.783 to 0.783 against 0.5, 0.25, 0.75, and the orthographic open floor 0.998 to 1.000. Sources: Jimenez,
Wu, Pesce and Jarabo 2016 (slices and the arc integral); Bavoil, Sainz and Dimitrov 2008 (horizon search in image
space); Max 1988 (a horizon over a height field, the height above the tangent plane as what occludes). Missing: other
GPUs.

**Covered scatter rings write coverage depth (KB-SCENES-DUNE-GTAO1, 2026-11-20, rendering).** Since
KB-SCATTER-SUBPIXEL1 `GrassScatter` blends its blades by prefiltered coverage with no depth write, and GTAO and SSAO
find occluders only in the depth buffer, so the grass stopped occluding the sand. Scatter now draws every covered ring
once more after all its blended draws, depth only (colour write mask 0, the same pose), keeping a fragment whose
coverage passes `scatterCover.w`; `GrassScatter` sets that to a hash of the blade, an object-space hashed alpha test of
the coverage (Wyman and McGuire 2017), so depth is present with the chance of the coverage and overlapping blades leave
a pixel bare with the chance over leaves its colour bare (Enderton, Sintorn, Shirley and Luebke 2010), stable as the
camera moves. Drawn last, the depth rejects no blended blade, so the colour and anti-aliasing are those of
KB-SCATTER-SUBPIXEL1. Post is unchanged. Evidence (Intel Arc 140V): scatter test/grass.test.js (the depth stage);
test/grass-pixel.browser.mjs on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (0 ppm speckle on WebGPU, means within 0.4 codes of the
supersampled view); scenes test/dune-coast-still.mjs camp view on the WebGL2 layer, mean 177.0 with occlusion against
180.6 without and 10.5 percent of pixels darker (before: 181.1 against 180.7, 0.4 percent); on native WebGPU
(2026-11-21, adapter `intel` `xe-2lpg`, once KB-SCENES-DUNE-ARCHANG1 below let it run) 177.2 against 180.6 and 10.2
percent darker. Missing: other GPUs, the cost of the extra draw (speed phase deferred), and the grass itself darkened
(it is not in the ambient replay).



Grass blade shadows (2026-11-27): `packages/scatter/test/grass-shadow.browser.mjs` reads the shadow `shadows.add(grass)`
casts from the picture on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (RTX A6000): a 2 m and a 4 m blade cast 2.05 m and 4.00 m,
narrowing 0.607 from 1 m to 3 m out against the blade's own 0.577, and 16 blades a clump shade 1,610 pixels against 91.
With the blade pose left out of the shadow pass the shadow runs 4.95 m at one width and the test fails. The same test
runs `VirtualShadows` (2.00 m and 4.05 m, narrowing 0.580, 1,501 pixels against 79) and a wind across the sun's way: in
both, 2.5 m from the root the shadow moves 0.59 m with the wind and lies within 0.02 m of where the sun throws the
blade's posed spine, read back with `readScatter`. It fails with the wind left out of the shadow pass, and with
`VirtualShadows` drawing no `drawShadow` caster. It also puts the blade in the middle and far rings, which are drawn by
coverage: each casts its own ring mesh (width 3 m over 1 m out 0.596 for two segments against 0.6, and 0.412 for one
against 0.333 in `Shadows`; 0.537 and 0.337 in `VirtualShadows`), and 48 thin blades shade 1,856 pixels against the near
ring's 1,844 (1,726 against 1,709 virtual). It fails with the shadow pass drawing the near ring alone. Missing: other
GPUs.

**No submission of the coastal flow's set-up holds the GPU for seconds (KB-SCENES-DUNE-ARCHANG1, 2026-11-21, GPU
behaviour).** The dune coast hung the device on a laptop GPU (DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG within 3 s, three runs of three).
Timestamp queries on every pass of the page's frames found one compute pass of 4,403 ms on the first frame: `Water`'s
coastal flow recorded its whole first-step set-up (initial state, connectivity, the surf field's width + height
relaxation sweeps, the 40 s spin-up of 3,600 flow dispatches; about 4,600 grid dispatches on a 512 x 512 map) into the
frame's one command buffer. Windows resets a GPU that cannot complete or preempt one DMA packet within 2 s (Microsoft,
"Timeout detection and recovery (TDR)" and "TdrDelay", Windows driver documentation), so it hung whenever the scheduler
asked to preempt it. `CoastalFlow.setUp` now records the same commands in order into command buffers of at most
`SETUP_WORKGROUPS` (2^18 workgroups, 64 dispatches of a 512 x 512 grid), one `queue.submit` each (Dawn merges the
buffers of one submit into one D3D12 command list), ahead of the frame's commands; the frame keeps its own three
substeps. The rule for any package: one-time GPU work of thousands of dispatches is submitted in bounded pieces, never in
the frame's command buffer. Evidence (adapter `intel` `xe-2lpg`, native WebGPU): 74 set-up submissions of at most 84 ms,
4.4 to 4.8 s of GPU time in all as before; water test/surf.browser.mjs (no first-frame submission over 2^18 workgroups,
at least the set-up's workgroups in all, run-up 0.126 m as before; fails before with one submission of 18,986,279) and
scenes test/dune-coast-still.mjs camp view passing. Missing: other GPUs, and a bound in time rather than workgroups (a
GPU 25 times slower than this one could still pass 2 s on one piece).

**No tanh in shader code takes an unbounded argument (KB-WATER-SURGEVOL1, 2026-11-21, GPU maths).** Native WebGPU on
an Intel xe-2lpg laptop GPU returns NaN for WGSL `tanh(x)` once sinh and cosh overflow f32 (measured: 1 at x = 50, NaN
at 100 and -100), while the WebGL2 layer ran the same surf without NaN. The surf's Ruessink et al. 2012 phase `tanh(0.815 / Ur^0.672)`
passes that in calm deep water (Ursell number under about 1e-3), so `surfSea` returned NaN, the open sea's relaxation
target `max(0, NaN)` read 0 and the sea next to the map's deep edge drained: water test/surge.browser.mjs held 1,431 of
the beach's 2,880 m^3 at rest. Every tanh in the surf's WGSL now takes `min(x, 10.0)`, which is exact in f32 (for x
over 9.01, 1 - tanh x is under 2^-25, so tanh rounds to 1; IEEE 754-2019 round to nearest). The rule for any package:
clamp a tanh argument to +-10 (or use an overflow-free form, as compute's `preciseTanh`); the WGSL implementation may
overflow inside. Evidence (adapter `intel` `xe-2lpg`): water test/surge.browser.mjs gives 2,880.15 m^3 at rest and
5,133.87 at a 1 m surge on native WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer alike, against the still-water 2,880 and 5,120 it now
asks for; water test/coast-runup.test.js fails on a bare tanh in water's sources. Open: blender's TANH math node
(KB-BLENDER-TANH1). Missing: other GPUs.

**SSAO's ambient replay binds every pass binding (KB-POST-GTAO-TERRAINLOOK1, 2026-11-18, GPU behaviour).** The replay
that gives SSAO and GTAO the ambient light to darken cut the lit shader from `let direct=` and bound a hand-picked
subset of the pass bindings (TAA's camera 18, sky ambient 8, the hemisphere light 144). A plugin binding read above
`let direct=` stayed in the replay's automatic layout but not in its bind group: TerrainColors' look uniform (41) gave
an invalid bind group and command buffer every frame. The replay now keeps the whole lit shader, the lighting in a dead
`if(false)` block (live with `margoAmbient`), and binds all of `c.bindings`, as SSGI's, SSR's and SceneTargets'
replays do; the output is the same ambient term. tests/shader-contracts.test.js fails on any package that filters a
pass context's bindings. Evidence (RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer, post test/replay-bindings-browser.mjs, 12
and 13 errors per case on the old code): a test plugin with a uniform above and one below `let direct=` under SSAO,
GTAO, SSGI, SSR, SceneTargets and a PostStack of GTAO, SSGI and SSR, and TerrainColors under GTAO, draw with no GPU
error; the scenes look-family check draws the terrain under the GTAO again. Missing: the replay's cost of the dead
code is left to the shader compiler (not measured; speed phase deferred).

## Cloud light: two-stream in the volumetric clouds (KB-CLOUD-DECKLIGHT1, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-17)

GPU maths change in `packages/sky/src/volumetric-clouds.ts`, both backends from one WGSL source. The source at each
cloud sample was three octaves of exp(-b od) (Wrenninge et al. 2013); it is now first-order scattering (forward
Henyey-Greenstein lobe on the delta-Eddington scaled beam, Joseph, Wiscombe and Weinman 1976; back lobe on the
unscattered beam) plus the two-stream diffuse field of a slab along the light (Meador and Weaver 1980; Bohren 1987) in
Eddington's angular form, from the optical depth toward the light and a three-sample column down to the base. Sky light
is a two-sided diffuse two-stream from the map's upper and lower halves plus the ground (`groundAlbedo` times the deck
share), summed so an even surround returns its own radiance; the cloud-shadows check, which needs exactly that, holds
its 0.006 bound. The deck now writes a second map, `Sky.environmentLightLayer`, which the sky's lighting reads, so the
sun the engine light already carries under `dimLight` is not added twice. Evidence: the `cloud-bounds` browser check
(RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` agree to 1e-3) measures hemispheric fluxes from the deck map against the
independent-column two-stream of the deck's own columns (Cahalan et al. 1994) at tau 5, 20 and 80, and the block under
stratus against the deck share; numbers in docs/known-bugs.md and docs/whitepaper/claims.md. Cost: three more
base-shape samples per lit cloud sample (frame times diagnostic only: 373, 7.8 and 12.0 ms ground, inside and above
against 354, 10.3 and 11.0 before, on a loaded machine). Missing: 3D transport (side leakage from finite clouds), a
reference renderer or photograph, and one unit for the sky map and the engine sun (KB-SKY-SUNUNITS1).

## Scud under a rain deck: two linked cloud layers (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-28)

GPU maths change in `packages/sky/src/volumetric-clouds.ts` and the lazy `packages/sky/src/scud-field.ts`, both
backends from one WGSL source. The `Clouds` uniform grows from 300 to 312 floats (`lift`: the `shear` lean and the scud
flag; `link` and `linkGlow`: the upper deck's transmittance of the sun, the moon and the sky light, the environment-map
order, the upper base's height and reflectance). `shear` adds a lean along the wind times height to every lookup of the
shared field (0 by default, so old pictures hold). A layer with `above` takes the sun, moon and sky light through the
upper deck's `cloudDeckTransmittance` and the upper base's reflectance of the ground lights back down; the upper layer
takes its ground lights through the lower layer's mean transmittance and draws its mist from the lower layer's tops up
(`cloudMistBand`). The upper layer's frame-graph pass draws both, in the camera's order (the upper first from under the
lower layer's tops). The scud shape is a lens profile on the unsharpened base with a calibrated cover map, shapes and
erosion stretched along the wind and the erosion warped by the shape volume. `volumetricCloudShadows` and `LightShafts`
take the scud shape with the layer. Evidence: `features-check.mjs scud` (RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` agree):
from between the layers looking up the frame is the deck's alone bit for bit, with and without mist; covered share
within 0.05 of `coverage` at 0.2, 0.35 and 0.6; edge per covered pixel 2.5 to 4 times a cumulus layer's at the same
share; the shapes move at the wind (the time-0 frame from a camera moved by wind x time matches best of 0, 0.5, 1 and
2 times); 7.6 times brighter toward a city than away; darker than the deck base with the sun up; in the mist each scud
pixel is its clear light times exp(-k s) to 0.1 percent. `cloud-layers.test.js` covers the link, names, deck product
and overlap; `cloud-shadows` and `shafts` checks still pass. Cost: no second layer, no added texture read; a scud layer
is one more march of 24 steps and 2 light steps. Missing: no mist inside the scud slab, the link is the decks' means
(no gap of the deck lights a shred more), and no photograph comparison is automated.

## Rain shafts under a deck (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-28)

GPU maths change in `packages/sky/src/volumetric-clouds.ts` and the lazy `packages/sky/src/rain-shafts.ts`, both
backends from one WGSL source. The `Clouds` uniform grows from 312 to 388 floats (`rain`: count, steps, band, fall,
wind, streaks; `rainCells`: up to 8 cells of centre, radius, rate, velocity and reach). Rain is a medium in the air
under the base, marched in the layer's air band to the scene depth (`sceneFar`): its rate at a point is each cell's
exponential mound at the base, read (base - h) / v seconds ago and (wind - cell velocity) times that upwind, with v the
fall speed of the strongest cell's median drop (Marshall and Palmer 1948 sizes, the Atlas, Srivastava and Sekhon 1973
fit), so the same law as `@margoengine/weather` `PrecipitationField.sample`. Extinction 3.647e-4 R^0.63 per metre; the
drops scatter the ground, deck, sun, moon and ground lights isotropically; a streak noise along the fall line breaks
the shaft into curtains. A lower layer with `above` draws the upper deck's rain from the ground through its own tops,
the upper from those tops to its base. The CPU twin (`cloudRainRate`, `rainRateAt`, `rainSource`) feeds `Weather`
`rainFrom` and `PrecipitationField`, so the rain round the camera is the rain the shafts draw there. Evidence:
`features-check.mjs rain-shaft` (RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, 4x and 1x): optical depth against the CPU
integral within 0.2 percent still, 0.3 wind, 0.5 moving cell, 0.2 split over two layers; a ray that misses the rain
keeps transmittance 0.998; clouds without rain bit-identical; a city light lights the shaft (0.019 against 0); streak
contrast 0.107 (bar 0.08). `rain-shafts.test.js` and `packages/weather/tests/rain-shaft-agree.test.js` hold the CPU
twin to the field. Cost: nothing for clouds without rain (the code loads by `import()`); with rain, 16 steps per pixel
in the air band. Missing: one fall speed per layer, isotropic phase, `WeatherDrive` does not pass its cells, and no
photograph comparison is automated.

KB-SKY-RAINSTEP1 (2026-11-28): the rain march's steps grow with distance (`cloudStepPower`, second step a quarter of the
smallest cell or ground light radius) with each sample stratified inside its own step, and each step takes the ground
lights' closed-form mean along its ground track (`cloudGroundTrack`) instead of one point: a 140 m lit yard under the
camera went from a neighbour difference of 0.68 of the mean to 0.008, its light the CPU integral to 0.2 percent
(`features-check.mjs rain-shaft` cases `yard` and `even`, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`). Case `even` records that the
drops and the deck are on one scale: under an overcast base lit by an even ground heavy rain keeps 1.15 times the
base's brightness. Cost: the same 16 steps, plus one closed-form track mean per ground light per step in place of a
point value.

## Cloud base lit from below: ground lights and mist (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-28)

GPU maths change in `packages/sky/src/volumetric-clouds.ts`, both backends from one WGSL source. `groundLights` (at
most eight discs of lit ground, 64 floats after the haze spots, the `Clouds` uniform now 300 floats) add to the light
from below each cloud sample takes into the two-stream (`cloudSkyScatter`'s lower side): a Lambertian disc of radius rho
on a plane H above it gives rho^2 / (H^2 + rho^2) of its radiance over its centre, falling as ((H^2 + rho^2) /
(H^2 + rho^2 + r^2))^2, which keeps the disc's flux, times the ground-to-deck series 1 / (1 - albedo x deck
reflectance) on the CPU (Kyba et al. 2011, Kocifaj 2007, Jechow and Holker 2019). `mist` (extinction 3.912 / visibility,
Koschmieder 1924) composites in front of the clouds over sky pixels only: flat Beer-Lambert to the base, its light the
isotropic single scattering of the mean radiance round it, the ground's (the even lower light plus the discs along the
ray's ground track to two extinction lengths, the closed-form line integral of the same law) and the deck's above.
Without either option the picture is unchanged: the added terms are zero and the fragment takes the old discards.
Evidence: `features-check.mjs ground-light` (RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` agree to 1e-4): a black deck
without light, 10 times brighter toward the city than away, structure (spread 0.33) overhead, the light's colour, the
mist 2.5 times brighter toward the city, and a disc wider than the sky equal to the even light from below to 1e-6;
`ground-light.test.js` proves the CPU twin's flux to 0.5 percent and the series. `volumetric`, `cloud-bounds` and
`overcast` still pass. Cost: one loop over the discs per lit cloud sample (none without them). Missing: the discs
are not shadowed by terrain or buildings, the mist is single scattering with an isotropic phase and a flat path, the
yard-scale light of a scene's own lamps on its mist near the camera is the scene fog's, and no photograph comparison
is automated.

## Sky light in the sun's units (KB-SKY-SUNUNITS1, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-17)

GPU maths change in `packages/sky/src/lighting.ts` (and the one `BlownSand` read of the sky map), both backends from one
WGSL source. The sky's light map was used in the sky model's own radiance units beside an engine sun in
`lighting.intensity`'s, so a clear sky lit level ground 1.3 to 1.5 times as much as the sun. `Sky.lightScale` (intensity
over the zenith sun on the ground in sky units: Preetham 4 pi x 0.55, Bruneton 20 x the zenith transmittance from
`zenithTransmittance` in atmosphere.ts) rides in the last float of the 160 B light buffer (`skyLight[9].w`) and scales
the harmonics and the reflection samples, never the ambient floor. Evidence: `packages/sky/test/sky-light-units-check.mjs`
(RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` agree to 1e-4): the sky's share of a level plate's light at 60 degrees is 0.184
(Preetham, bound 0.1 to 0.2, Erbs, Klein and Duffie 1982) and 0.064 (Bruneton, bound 0.04 to 0.1, Bird and Hulstrom
1981), within 0.01 from intensity 1 to 3. Cost: no new pass, buffer or binding; one float in an existing upload.

**The sky's picture in the same units (KB-SKY-SANDGREY1 and KB-SKY-PALLHAZE1, 2026-11-27).** The light map was in the
sun's units but the picture was not: the backdrop, fog, reflection map and the layers drawn over the sky in sky units
(VolumetricClouds, AerialPerspective, LightShafts, TornadoCloud) stood 1.4 times too bright against the ground under the
presets' Preetham sun of 5, about 6 times under Bruneton at 3. `Sky.pictureScale` (lightScale by day while the sky
lights the scene, fading to 1 with the night blend; `balance: false` keeps 1) is added to the exposure float the sky's
backdrop, environment and fog shaders already read, and the light buffer's scale becomes lightScale / pictureScale, so
the map is scaled once; the layers take it with the exposure they read. WeatherDrive's haze colour, a share where 1 is
the zenith sun on a white surface, is drawn as that share times `Sky.zenithSun` over pi at the sky's exposure and
picture scale, the units the sky draws the same layer's `scatteredLight` in. No WGSL changed: two floats in existing
uploads. Evidence: sky test/sky.test.js and weather tests/smoke.test.js (the uniforms and the colour);
sky-light-units-check.mjs unchanged on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (shares 0.18 and 0.06: the map is not scaled twice);
real scene stills before and after in docs/known-bugs.md. Missing: a photograph-referenced ratio of a clear horizon sky
to sunlit ground in a GPU check.

**The haze below the horizon along the actual ray (KB-SKY-HAZEBELOW1, 2026-11-27).** The sky fog took the horizon's
radiance (the ray's y clamped to 0.0001) for every ray below it, so a far ground the haze hides fully drew as one flat
colour. A ray going down meets haze deeper in the layer, lit by e^(-k tau) of the light at the eye at vertical optical
depth tau (the two-stream diffusion mode, Meador and Weaver 1980); in a horizontally uniform layer the vertical optical
depth to a point is sin(down) times the ray's, whatever the height profile, so the in-scatter of a ray of optical depth
x is the eye's haze colour times (1 - e^(-x (1 + c))) / ((1 + c) (1 - e^(-x))), c = k sin(down): one closed form in
the fog fragment (`fogBelowLight`), its k in one new uniform vec4 (`fog.lightDecay`, default 0, where the factor is
exactly 1). `WeatherDrive` writes k from the load's albedos and asymmetries (`hazeLightDecay`). In-scatter along the
actual view ray follows Hillaire 2020 and Bruneton and Neyret 2008. Evidence: sky test/fog-below-check.mjs on WebGPU and
`MARGO_COMPAT=1` (RTX A6000, ANGLE D3D11): the hazed ground's ratio to no decay matches the CPU mirror to 8.4e-4 and
is 0.39 off without the shader term; the ridge-smoke shot's pre-dither float flat 10.06 to 6.44 percent early and 5.82
to 2.73 mid against main. Missing: the change of the phase angle to the sun between the horizon and the actual ray, and
shadows in the air (cloud and smoke-column shadows).

**Fog past the scene's end (KB-SKY-BAREBELOW1, 2026-11-28).** The fog pass discarded every pixel with no depth, so
where a world ended before the horizon (its edge, or a camera far plane short of the far ground) the sky's own horizon
colour showed under the far ranges as a flat band, unlike the fogged ground beside it. A bare pixel above the horizon is
still the sky's; one below it takes the fog at infinity (opacity 1, colour times `fogBelowLight` for a hidden ground,
no fire haze), the limit of in-scattering as optical depth grows (Bruneton and Neyret 2008). Evidence: sky
test/fog-below-check.mjs on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (RTX A6000, ANGLE D3D11): with the ground gone, 31,966 pixels
below the horizon match the fog colour to 6.0e-4 and the 16,128 sky pixels are unchanged. Fingerprints fog and
fogColour and traces night-fog, afterlight and preetham-clouds-fog recorded again (WGSL text only).

**Rock facets filtered by footprint (terrain `rock`, 2026-11-28).** Jointed blocks 200 to 600 m off drew as low-poly
shards: each Worley cell's tilt switched hard at its edge and kept full relief and joint shade while a block spanned 10
to 60 pixels. The tilt and tone now blend into the second-nearest cell's by F2 - F1 (over 0.14 of a cell plus two
pixels) and relief, tone and joint shade fall to 0.3 between footprints of 0.006 and 0.04 of a block (Toksvig 2005;
Bruneton and Neyret 2012). Evidence: terrain test/rock-structure.browser.mjs on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`: 16 m blocks
47 pixels across jump in tone between neighbouring pixels 0.003 of the time (0.027 before) at an sd of 11 (22 before),
and a close view keeps its spread. Missing: sub-block weathering texture within a facet.

**The fires' light on the smoke layer at every hour (KB-SKY-FIREDAY1, 2026-11-27).** The look's `lowLayer` added the
fires' light on the layer (`atmosphere.fireSpots`) by the night's share alone, while the sky fog adds the same fires'
light to the haze (`fog.fireSpots`) at every hour, so by day a fully hazed far ridge read lighter than the sky over it
(timber-valley ridge, 23, 12 and 4 codes). `fireLayer` is now added at every hour, and `VolumetricClouds` above the layer
take it in front through their veil (the `Clouds` uniform grows from 104 to 168 floats for the eight spots); one WGSL
source (`fireLayerWgsl`) serves both. Evidence: sky features-check look on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (a day fire spot
raises the frame in the fire's colour; [0, 0, 0] without the fix), the ridge still 4, 1 and -1 codes against the sky.
**The haze's fire glow on the sky's own rays (KB-SKY-HAZEGLOW1, 2026-11-27).** The fog drew a far ground as the sky's
radiance plus the fires' glow on the haze (`fireHaze`, the mean of the falloff along the ground path to 2 / density),
and the sky over it the layer's glow at one point (`fireLayer`), so a fully hazed ridge stood 6 codes lighter than the
sky (timber-valley valley-aerial mid banding 0.227 percent: the ridge line, both sides flat). `fireSky` in
`fire-spots.ts` now draws the layer's glow through the haze under it (t, the low layer's transmittance along the ray)
and the haze's glow in front (1 - t) by the fog's own closed form (`fireTrackWgsl`, one source for both; the fog's WGSL
text is unchanged), with the fog's spots in the look block (`LOOK_FLOATS` 144 to 208) and the `Clouds` uniform (168
to 232 floats). Evidence: sky features-check look on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, the same pixels over the sky and over
a fully hazed plane 50 km out agreeing exactly (0.52 relative without the fix). The night's base light at the horizon
(the fog took the night sky, the dome sees it through the layer) was fixed the same day by `hazeLayer`
(KB-SKY-NIGHTRIDGE1): the fog passes its sky colour through the layer and its glow, without the fires, which it adds
itself; `features-check.mjs look` `nightRidge` pins it on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.

**Lit particles: the ambient from above, the air from below (KB-VFX-SMOKEFLAT1, 2026-11-27).** GPU maths change in
`packages/vfx/src/lit.ts`, both backends from one WGSL source. A lit billboard took its ambient and the air's light
(`VFXLit.air`) alike from every side, so a dense smoke column drew one flat colour. The shader now splits both by the
isotropic view factors (1 + n_y) / 2 and (1 - n_y) / 2 (Liu and Jordan 1963; Meador and Weaver's two-stream split,
1980): the ambient A as 2A / (1 + g) from above and g of that from below (`ground`, default 0.2), the air S as
2S / (1 + R) from below and R of that from above (`airReflectance`, default `PALL_REFLECTANCE`; `WeatherDrive` writes
`hazeReflectance`), each mean kept. The lit uniform grows from 96 to 128 bytes (`air`, `airBack`; the ground albedo in
`ambient.w`). Evidence: `features-check.mjs` `checkLit` on an RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, 1x and 4x, every
third pixel within 1.13/255 of the CPU split; `lit-check.mjs` unchanged on both; timber-valley ridge-smoke early flat
7.60 to 2.45 percent. Missing: self-shadowing inside a column, per-puff noise, timing. The same day the drive's
`atmosphere.fireSight` became 2 / the sky fog's own density (KB-WEATHER-FIRESIGHT1), matching the fog's fire track
under an `'exp2'` fog.

## Overcast deck on the sky cloud sheet (KB-SKY-OVERCAST1, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-17)

GPU maths change in `packages/sky/src/clouds.ts`, both backends from one WGSL source. At full cover the 2D sheet kept
its noise holes, 1 - exp(-3 density) let the sun disc and its glow through, and past 40 km of haze it returned the
clear sky (a brown band at the horizon). From 80 to 100 percent cover the sheet now closes into `cloudDeck`: the CIE
overcast gradation (Moon and Spencer 1942; CIE S 011/E:2003 type 1) of the two-stream transmission
1 / (1 + 0.075 depth) (Meador and Weaver 1980; Bohren 1987) of the sun on its top, in the sky model's units (Preetham
4 pi x 0.55, Bruneton 20 x the zenith transmittance), carried in the free `moonColor.w` float of the Frame uniform. The
engine sun fades by the same smoothstep (`overcastShare`). Evidence: `features-check.mjs overcast` on an RTX A6000,
WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` alike, every pixel within 0.92 to 1.09 of the CPU twin `overcastDeck`. Cost: one more
branch and four noise lookups per sky pixel above 80 percent cover; no new pass, buffer or binding.
KB-SKY-OVERCAST2 (2026-11-24, Fauld recut): the deck's top was lit in the sun's colour alone (the clear sky's share a
scalar 1 / (1 - 0.165) of the sun), so a 4 to 15 degree sun turned the deck, the SH ambient and the fog orange-brown.
The top now takes the sun on level ground plus the clear sky's own E / pi, `clearSkyLevel`: three-point Gauss-Legendre
in sin^2 of the zenith angle times an eight-point azimuth trapezoid about the sun's vertical, mirrored (15 daySky
evaluations; within 6 percent of a dense integral of the Preetham reference, 2 to 80 degree suns, turbidity 2 and 6).
The clear term is in the model's own units: the Bruneton deck divides it by its units, recomputed in the shader by the
CPU's 64-step zenith column through the sky's extinction, so no uniform changed. The fog reads the same
`overcastLight`. Evidence: `features-check.mjs overcast`, RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, every pixel within
0.93 to 1.10 of the twin fed the clear sky read from the GPU at the rule's directions; test/overcast.test.js (deck blue
over red 0.78 to 0.89 under a 4 to 15 degree sun at turbidity 3, against 0.09 to 0.55 before). Cost: 15 day-sky
evaluations and a 64-step column per deck pixel and per fog pixel under clouds; a per-frame table would remove it
(not built: it needs a binding in every sky pipeline).

## Hurricanes in the volumetric clouds, and haze by the air crossed (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-17)

GPU maths change in `packages/sky/src/volumetric-clouds.ts`, both backends from one WGSL source. The `Clouds` uniform
grew from 64 to 96 floats (`CLOUD_FLOATS`; the clouds, their shadows and shafts share it) with eight `storm` vectors.
While a storm is set (`hurricane` option or `type: 'hurricane'`), `cloudDensityAt` takes `cloudStormDensity`: the
storm's cover (`cloudStormCover`: eye, eyewall leaning out at `eyeSlope`, moat, outer eyewall, log-spiral bands,
shield, canopy, each with its own top) replaces the coverage map's, and the base noise is read twice, at the point
turned back about the storm centre by the Holland gradient wind over radius times each of two flow-map phases half a
`flowPeriod` apart (Vlachos 2010), cross-faded, and carried with the storm's travel. The CPU twin is
`hurricaneCover` in `packages/sky/src/hurricane.ts` (the same formulas, used by `Hurricane.coverAt`, `windAt`,
`rainAt`, `weatherAt` and the deck's dimming over the camera). The haze on cloud light changed for every layer: it was
exp(-t / 40 km) of the ray's length; it is exp(-A / 40 km) with A the sea-level-equivalent air the ray crosses, its
length times the mean of exp(-height / 8 km) between the eye and the sample (straight-ray air mass of an exponential
atmosphere); a ground camera's near cloud is hazed within a few percent of before, an aircraft's far cloud far less.
Evidence: `features-check.mjs hurricane` on an RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`: every pixel whose ray the CPU
field says crosses no cloud stays at the background, every one crossing solid eyewall or band is lit, from 40 km and
90 km up and from sea level in the eye; the 90 km view keeps over 0.8 of the 40 km view's light (0.91 measured; about a
quarter with the old haze); the eye moves 6 km in 600 s at 10 m/s within 1.5 km. Cost while a storm is drawn: one more
shape read per sample and one more erosion read per view sample. Missing: a reference renderer or satellite image
comparison, storm motion asymmetry in the wind, mesovortices and polygonal eyes.

## Tornadoes: funnel, wall cloud and debris (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-18)

`@margoengine/sky/tornado` holds the CPU model (`Tornado`: Burgers-Rott or modified Rankine wind, cyclostrophic pressure, the condensation
funnel's radius at each height by bisection on the deficit, the debris edge, the path, the spin-up, the weather and the damage path) and
`TornadoCloud`, a full-screen pass at frame-graph order 3.5 (after the clouds, before the aerial perspective). Its WGSL lives in
`packages/sky/src/tornado-shader.ts` and loads by import() at the first frame (`scripts/lazy-files.js` records the split). The pass
marches each view ray through a vertical cylinder round the storm with a distance-based step (small near the funnel's axis, large in the
wall cloud), reads the funnel's radius from a 32-height table the CPU fills each frame from the same `funnelRadius`, takes three density
reads toward the sun per lit sample, and writes premultiplied light and transmittance (dst times alpha plus src), so it composes over the
scene and the cloud deck. With `depth` the march stops at the scene.

Evidence: `features-check.mjs tornado` on an RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, 4x and 1x: rays that come near nothing of the storm
stay exactly at the background, rays deep inside the CPU funnel are lit (tenth percentile above 0.8 of the sun's units), the funnel's
width 150 m up within a quarter of the CPU's for a rope (4 px against 3.3), a strong funnel (10 against 10.6) and a wedge (38 against
36.8), the funnel 395 m along a 400 m path, and a 45 hPa funnel hanging at 201 m over black ground. Missing: no comparison with a
photograph or a reference renderer; the look is judged on whole-scene frames by the films.

## Skin from melanin and blood (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-18)

`@margoengine/materials/skin` gains the two-layer spectral skin of Donner and Jensen 2006 (`skin-spectrum.ts`): absorption
from melanin and hemoglobin (Prahl's measured spectra), multipole diffusion per layer added in the frequency domain, the
spectrum to linear sRGB, and its profile fitted by non-negative least squares with d'Eon and Luebke's six Gaussians plus
two narrower ones. `skin({ melanin, ... })` builds its pre-integrated table and its through-the-part term from that fit;
without the four numbers nothing changes. Evidence: `skin-measured.test.js` (Jensen 2001 measured Rd within 0.012, the
hemoglobin bands, the ColorChecker skin patches within 8.6 and 6.1 CIELAB, the fit within 0.025 of the Bessel-transformed
model profile, the published fit within a factor of 2 for fair skin and more than five times too wide at melanin 0.3,
Christensen and Burley 2015 within a factor of 2.5); `features-browser.mjs skin` on an RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2
layer, a 5 mm sphere at melanin 0.3 within an 8-bit step and 1% of its own table. Missing: a comparison with measured
face skin spectra or a photograph; single scattering and the oil layer.

## Eye optics and tear film (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-18)

`@margoengine/materials/eye` refracts the view and light rays on the cornea's own sphere (`corneaRadius`, default 0.65 of
the globe, 7.8 mm of 12, apex on the mesh's) to an iris plane 3.6 mm behind the apex (`depth` 0.3), and lays a tear film
(index 1.337) over the whole front: over the cornea it is the front's index, over the white a smooth GGX coat with the
cornea's roughness that takes its Fresnel share from the rough lobe below (`wetness`, live). Evidence:
`features-browser.mjs eye`, RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer: Le Grand's entrance pupil magnification 1.133 within
0.015 by the trace the frame matches within 2.5 pixels, and a point-like catchlight on the white at the mirror point.
Slider rows: `@margoengine/materials/settings`. Missing: a comparison with a photograph of a living eye, the corneal bulge
in silhouette, and a measured limbus.

## Scene sky on glTF and FBX models (KB-GLTF-SCENESKY1, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-18)

Core meshes take a lighting `Sky`'s ambient through the scene shader patch (`sky:environment`), but a glTF or FBX model
(`@margoengine/gltf/pbr` `PBRModel`, which FBX, `stage/gltf` and the CC reader all produce) drew its own shader with the
flat built-in sky and ground gradient unless the caller wrote `sky.add(model)`. Nothing in the films did, so outfits, the
flyer and every prop read warm and flat beside the sky-lit ground (the cause of Wilbur's orange skin, fixed for people
alone in 6a604a13cc). `PBRModel` now joins its scene's `'sky'` plugin before each draw (`sceneSky`, default true) once
the sky has an ambient, through the same `sky.add` path, and leaves when the sky goes, the model is disposed or the model
is given its own ambient (`environment.add`, light probes, another sky), keeping one ambient term per shader as core's
patch does. Core and stage are untouched (24,841 B gzip). Evidence, RTX A6000, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`:
`sky-environment-check.mjs` (a glTF box with no `sky.add` draws the same frames as with it and matches the core box
within 0 of 255; `sceneSky` false keeps the old warm 157, 155, 152 against 157, 157, 161; the HDR environment still owns
an `env.add` model), `sky-add-gltf-check.mjs` (no `sky.add` draws the `sky.add` frames from frame 0, still and in rain),
`person-still.mjs` (under the overcast preset, roughness 0.3 against 0.8 changes 7,690 pixels of an outfit and 1,265 of
the Lantern prop with no `sky.add`, 0 with `sceneSky` false). Missing: `VoxelRenderer`, the other target of `sky.add`, still needs
the call; no comparison of a sky-lit prop with a photograph yet (the films judge it on whole-scene frames).

## Lid shadow anchored to the visible lid margin (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-18)

`@margoengine/fbx/character-creator` draws Character Creator's eye occlusion shell (`RLEyeOcclusion`) as a lid shadow
from the shader's numbers, measured down from the shell's top edge. That edge tucks under the lid skin, so the darkest
part lay where no camera sees it. The reader's `scene` hook now finds the margin the head's skin leaves visible: a ray
from each shell vertex along the shell's area-weighted outward normal against the `RLHead` skin triangles (Moller and
Trumbore, "Fast, Minimum Storage Ray-Triangle Intersection", JGT 1997, https://doi.org/10.1080/10867651.1997.10487468),
bisection on the shell edges between hidden and seen vertices, and a per-u remap of the shell's v so the margin is v 0.
Why darkest at the margin: ambient occlusion by the lid and lashes (Zhukov, Iones and Kronin, "An Ambient Light
Illumination Model", EGWR 1998; Jimenez, von der Pahlen et al., "Next-Generation Character Rendering", GDC 2013). No
published measurement of upper-sclera darkening was found (Wood et al., "Rendering of Eyes for Eye-Shape Registration
and Gaze Estimation", ICCV 2015, and the GDC talk give none), so it was measured on a CC0 photograph of a frontal eye
(Wikimedia Commons, "A human male brown eye.jpg", Bobbyphotographer 2025; asset library references/eyes/LABEL.md, never
in git): sclera luminance over its middle at 0.15 in the first twentieth under the margin, 0.25, 0.42, 0.55, 0.69 and
0.80 in the next five (41 columns, linear Rec. 709). Evidence: `packages/fbx/test/eye-margin.test.js` (margin within
0.01 of the shell; the shadow at the margin 0.620 against Character Creator's 0.624, 0.064 before; never darker than
the photograph's 25th percentile from the margin down; at least half its margin darkening). On Wilbur's FBX the
margin sits at v 0.03 to 0.09 across the eye, at the corners 0.16 to 0.5; after the remap the margin measures within
0.01 of v 0 across the middle 16 of 24 columns. Missing: the corner bins keep up to 0.46 (the top shadow narrows to nothing there
by its Arc); the rest of the photograph's darkening (the ball's own shading, the lashes) is left to the eye material
and the lash cards, judged on the film's frames.

## Water planar capture edges

The optional `@margoengine/water/reflector` adapter blends finite planar captures
into the underlying sky reflection at the projected edge. The per-axis blend width
covers the roughness filter and the maximum authored wave offset. The same shader
runs on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer. The browser fixture spans a known
finite capture edge and verifies the sky outside, rising reflection across the
transition and the full reflection inside. See the [clean-room record](../clean-room.md#water-planar-capture-edges-2026-11-24).

The package runner gives each browser suite its own ten-minute process limit.
The Water manifest separates flood and underwater checks, optics and flow
checks, and surface and ship checks into three suites. Its original command chain
exceeded the group limit on the WebGL2 path while passing cases in order. The
suite split keeps each existing browser case and both underwater capture modes,
with unchanged assertions and per-suite deadlines. The manifest coverage
regression is in `packages/water/test/browser-root.test.js`.

## Soft bodies (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-24)

`@margoengine/physics/soft` runs on its own Rust crate, `packages/physics/soft-kernel`, compiled to Wasm with SIMD, built by `packages/physics/scripts/build-soft-kernel.mjs` into the committed blueprint `src/soft-wasm.ts` (a chunk of its own, loaded by `SoftBodies.attach`). The step path uses only addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, square root, comparisons and integer operations, so two runs end in the same state (`tests/soft.test.js`, and the crate's `a_step_is_bit_for_bit_the_same`). Evidence: a rope pinned at both ends matches the catenary in sag and per-particle height within 3% and 0.06 m, a soft edge oscillates at its natural frequency within 4% for masses 0.1 to 25 (`soft-kernel/tests/rope.rs`), a swinging rope never gains energy, a particle resting on a half space loads its body with its weight (`soft-kernel/tests/contact.rs`), a cloth pinned along an edge hangs its full length, and a box on a cloth sinks it more as it gets heavier. Tetrahedral cells are in the same kernel (`soft-kernel/src/fem.rs`): stable Neo-Hookean (Smith, de Goes and Kim 2018) or co-rotated elasticity as XPBD constraints on the deformation gradient, plastic flow by a multiplicative split folded into the rest shape, tearing by removing a cell, and shape-matching clusters as implicit springs. Evidence (`soft-kernel/tests/fem.rs`, `tests/soft-cells.test.js`): a cantilever's tip sag reaches 55, 88 and about 99 percent of Euler-Bernoulli's as its mesh goes from 8 by 2 to 12 by 3 to 16 by 4 cells, a Poisson's ratio of 0.49 keeps the volume within 3 percent under a 30 percent stretch, a plastic beam keeps a set, a bar torn past its threshold is two pieces, a twisted block with a cluster returns within 0.1 mm, and a run replays bit for bit. Missing: speed (build phase), cuts that split a body into new bodies, and the other rows of the parity document.

Soft bodies meet rigid bodies two ways, in the soft step (2026-11-24): the rigid kernel finds each particle's contacts (swept, `probe.rs`) and each triangle's (`face.rs`: conservative advancement on the GJK distance of the moving triangle to each convex piece, then the triangle's contact manifold), once a step, each with what the collider's surface is there (`contact_feature`: a face, told by where the support goes as the direction turns about the normal, or the radius of curvature of a round place, corner or edge). The soft kernel holds them through its pieces as position constraints (Mueller et al. 2007 for the point and triangle, Mueller et al. 2020 for the body's generalized inverse mass and its rotation update, the turn a normalised quaternion), a face by its plane turning with the body and a round place from its centre of curvature, the body's inertia turned with it, then makes the contacts the position pass pushed on inelastic with Coulomb friction. The rigid body takes the push as an impulse at the start of the rigid step and a force over it, solved so the rigid kernel's substeps (semi-implicit Euler) carry a free body to where the soft step took it, and its spin as the change the soft step gave it. Evidence: a 26 g box, a thin rod, a 1 cm bead and a 1 kg box on a ringing default cloth stay on it for 330 steps, each over the sheet under it; boxes at mass ratios of a thousand either way are held, and a cloth with a tear strain tears under a tonne (`tests/soft.test.js`); a ball pressed into a triangle is pushed out along its normal in one solve with momentum kept and no turn, a rod's contact that slid round it gives no spin about its axis, a body's inertia turns with it, and a turn past a tenth of a radian is a rotation (`soft-kernel/tests/face.rs`, `turn.rs`); the face query meets a ball over a triangle's inside, a fast triangle at its first touch, and tells faces, edges, corners and round places apart (`tests/soft-faces.test.js`). Missing: contacts found more than once a step (a body that turns far within a step), and speed (build phase).

Skeletal soft tissue (SOFT-05, `physics/src/tissue.ts`). The optional adapter drives the existing native soft
step from the layout-2 rigid bodies field. Fixed insertions use the particle kinematic target. Sliding skin uses
the local normal and its rigid point velocity, then delivers a backward Euler normal impulse to the particle.
The parent body handle guards lifetime and rejects a switch to a dynamic bone. Coupling is one-way for the
prescribed skeleton. Rigid contact outside the prescribed skeleton uses the inherited soft-body ports.
The CPU fixture checks actual rigid transforms, exact snapshot replay, analytic normal compliance and zero tangent
load. WebGPU and WebGL2 render the simulated tissue surface and compare the normal and tangential controls.
A conforming tetrahedral mesh can carry independent reversible Neo-Hookean coefficients and density per cell.
The native step sums all incident cell contributions at each shared particle. Both cut routes carry the parent
law and use density-weighted material support to distribute nodal mass. Exact coupon and cut proofs cover those
paths. Active contraction and held-out deformation measurements remain open.

The optional finite-chain rubber branch evaluates first and second strain invariants in the native cell solve
and checks each nonlinear vertex update against the full implicit objective. The authored curve words live
with the native cell state so a world snapshot includes them. Exact derivative, inversion and replay checks
pass. The measured traction fixture covers the withheld finite-strain Treloar data and records the small
biaxial tension error. Independent large-deformation gelatin and ice evidence is pending.

Cloth tethers (2026-11-27, `soft-kernel/src/tether.rs`, test `tests/soft-tethers.test.js`). Long range attachments (Kim, Chentanez and Mueller 2012): three tether columns (`tt_p`, `tt_a`, `tt_len`) hold each tied particle, its pin and its allowed distance; once per pass of `substep_pre`, after the edges, a particle with weight farther from its pin than that distance is set on the sphere around the pin (one square root, a ratio, three multiplications: the step's pinned operations). The ties are written from TypeScript (Dijkstra over the structural and shear rest lengths) when a body, a pin, a tear or a stretch changes, never each step. Evidence: a 2 by 10 m sheet solved with one pass a step stretches 0.65 percent untied and none tied, a slack rope tied and untied ends bit for bit the same, and a tear or a new pin ties the particles again. Missing: a GPU path (all soft solving is CPU Wasm), speed (build phase).

Skinned cloth (2026-11-27, `soft-kernel/src/skin.rs`, test `tests/soft-skinned-cloth.test.js`). Twelve skin columns (`sk_p`, the skinned point and its speed over the step, the skin's normal, `sk_max`, `sk_back`) are written from TypeScript each step for the particles with a finite max distance or a backstop; the kernel carries the points on by `h` times their speed at the start of each piece and projects the particles inside their spheres and in front of their backstops each pass and once after the exact thread solve. A max distance of 0 is a pinned particle with a target (the existing kinematic path). Evidence: a cape on a running, turning character holds its limits to 1e-5 m over 240 steps; free below its pinned row it is bit for bit a pinned cloth. Missing: a GPU path, speed (build phase).
