GPU cloth CPU route (2026-11-27, `packages/physics/cloth-kernel`, `src/cloth/kernel.ts`, tests `tests/gpu-cloth.test.js`, `tests/gpu-cloth-check.mjs`). The WebGL2 compatibility layer and Node step `GPUCloth` in a Rust kernel built with SIMD (`cloth-kernel.wasm`, 10,941 B, its own memory per cloth, stateless: no data section, no bounds-check panic locations), running the WGSL passes of `gpu-cloth-shaders.ts` in the same order with f64 arithmetic on f32 state (sin and cos its own, Cody and Waite reduction). It replaced the TypeScript twin: a 33 by 33 cloth over a ball and the ground, 20 to 8.5 ms a step in Node on the loaded laptop (not a gate). Evidence: every GPU cloth closed-form test on it; the WebGPU route within 1e-4 m of it after a step; exact work counts (`stats.work`). Missing: threads, speed against the rival (build phase).

Cloth vertex blocks (2026-11-27, `soft-kernel/src/cloth_block.rs`, test `tests/soft-cloth-vertex-block.test.js`). An edge flag, `BLOCK` (16), marks the edges of a body of edges on the vertex-block solver: the sweep and the exact solve leave them, and each pass solves every particle's 3 by 3 block (inertia plus its springs, positive-definite by the squeezed-spring projection) by LDL^T in f64, writing f32 positions. Three particle columns (`cbx`, `cby`, `cbz`) hold the velocity before gravity at the last piece, for the adaptive first guess; they are state (snapshots and hashes carry them) and are compacted with the other particle columns when a body is removed. Evidence: Irvine's cable sag within 0.1 percent at 2 and 8 passes; a soft edge's period within 2 percent; bit-for-bit replay. Missing: graph-coloured parallel blocks, a GPU path, speed (build phase).

Volumetric vertex blocks (SOFT-04, `soft-kernel/src/vertex_block.rs`). The deterministic incident-corner list
is rebuilt from the live tetrahedra, so tears retire their cells from the next solve. Inertia and exact local
elastic Hessians accumulate in f64 for an LDLᵀ solve. Positions use the existing f32 columns. The mode is saved
with the particle and tetrahedron flags, using the existing snapshot layout. The soft and rigid world ports
carry the rung's reaction. Rust exact tests, world replay and both browser renderers cover the path.
Vertex sweeps use deterministic serial Gauss–Seidel and existing split contact passes.

The native Projective Dynamics alternative projects each cell's local gradient before solving one
constant-operator global system per iteration. The solve reuses preconditioned conjugate gradients
with three coordinates and a scalar diagonal per vertex. It works in corrections to the inertial
prediction and leaves fixed targets out of the unknowns. The same rung proof checks its reactions,
frame-rate independence and restore, and both renderers draw the changed geometry.

Directional reinforcement contributes one right-axis projection per active fiber and keeps the
same global stiffness operator within each substep. The local vertex mode adds the corresponding
diagonal to its surrogate Hessian. Both use the optional native rest-space axis and modulus rows.
Snapshot restore, body compaction and fracture retain those rows. Isotropic worlds retain their
earlier state layout.

Full orthotropic elasticity (`soft-kernel/src/orthotropic.rs`) uses the three normal and three
engineering shear components of Green strain in the authored material frame. A symmetric tensor
maps strain to stress. Each vertex block applies the strain derivatives, adds a determinant-based
compression force and backtracks against the full local objective. Each accepted update lowers
or preserves that objective at the stored precision. The five public tests compare the axial and
shear responses to independent equations, recover an inverted tetrahedron, reject malformed material
inputs and check snapshot and cut retention. The LH-4 browser fixture renders a loaded orthotropic
rung, with the rigid reaction and deterministic replay through the same world ports.

Plane cuts clip each affected tetrahedron, use one intersection vertex per old edge, and
triangulate shared faces using the same global vertex order on each side. Each child rest basis
is carried by the parent-to-child affine map. The cut prepares every descriptor and preflights
its masses and geometry before replacing the old body. Linear momentum is transferred with
the same weights as mass. The optional native tear load joins the snapshot whenever
smoothed fracture is active and is copied instead of reset during cut or body compaction.
The browser fixture cuts the loaded LH-4 rung into two meshes and follows the changed boot
position in both renderers.

Plane cuts, finite incisions and face tears carry each live point attachment to the mapped copies
of its original material vertex. A stretched attachment keeps the same rigid-local point. The
coupled regression applies force on a cut fragment and measures motion of the linked rigid body
while both duplicate points remain attached.

The vertex-block step solves free translation once after its local elastic sweeps and before the
rigid rows. Moving every point by the mass-weighted inertial residual minimizes the inertial
objective while leaving the elastic strain unchanged. This preserves the linear impulse of
free, damped fragments through rigid attachment coupling at a fixed iteration count.

An authored deformable surface collider is rebuilt from each resulting piece's live boundary
before the source collider is removed. A ray can see the cut immediately and again after the
body moves. The replacement inherits the live contact, query and event settings, including
changes since the body was authored.

A tensile seam evaluates normal Green strain in its intact tetrahedron after native contact.
The seam rides the cell in affine coordinates. When the prescribed positive opening is exceeded,
the finite cut builds real separate lips, transfer preserves linear momentum, and the common
tear event reports the source cell. An intact snapshot replays the same opening and state hash.
Authored weak patches may set independent sliding and tearing limits. The material-frame
normal and both shear terms share a quadratic strain envelope before geometry is opened.

The unseeded option scans the existing native cell state after contact, bounds the maximum
strain and diagonalizes the surviving symmetric tensors. The principal direction orients the
exact centroid section of the most stretched cell. The inherited native flag suppresses
repeat nucleation in that material region and leaves all uncracked neighbors eligible.
The remesher shares the split faces and edges with incident neighbors. The matching facets
keep the mesh closed, and remote tetrahedra stay at their original resolution.
For propagation, a supercritical cell at the existing front projects its principal direction
into the plane perpendicular to that edge. The new section starts at the old front. Its
midpoint separates when the front advances, and the registered replacement facets keep the
two lips continuous. Advancing retires the previous edge in all incident cells. The active
edge slots are included in native snapshot state.
An explicit finite cut can seed that same progression. The material face before release
identifies the two lips, and their common pair of particle IDs identifies the bonded edge.
The native selector can also nominate a bonded face that lies in the propagation plane.
The remesher opens the shared facet and only refines cells on its former front edge.
An optional native mode instead compares each available coplanar facet to an authored
mixed toughness. It obtains the opening and the two shears from the actual separated
particles at a matching rest point. Per-body incident-corner scratch is reused between
steps. No new permanent particle or cell columns enter the snapshot layout.
The fracture step checks the rounded rest mesh before it replaces live topology. The LH-4
overload fixture starts fracturing on step 4 under a 122.86 N rigid contact reaction and
replays 15 cut events by step 18, while the same test threshold keeps the bare rung intact.

Orthotropic fracture evaluates material-frame stress after native elasticity and contact. It
filters tensile, compressive and shear utilization separately. That optional state follows
cells through body compaction, both cut paths, and world snapshots. The existing tear scheduler
uses the highest active utilization to separate overloaded cells without losing their mass.
The beech fixtures bracket published axial means and verify all three shear channels, including
an automatically separated pair of cells.

Progressive timber damage adds crack-band work per area before tensile or shear fracture.
Native tests integrate the complete shear response at two element lengths and verify that a
closed tensile crack recovers compressive capacity. The irreversible damage and load signs
are held fixed during each local solve. Public tests exercise partial damage, fracture and
snapshot replay during a topology change, with a physical mesh resolution check at creation.

Finite tetrahedral incisions keep shared cap edges conforming and duplicate particle slots
only across blade-covered faces. A triangle completely inside one cell creates two independent
surfaces and leaves the material connected at the crack front. Tests check area, volume,
closed boundaries, real movement under a load on one lip, and replay through world snapshots.

Exact cloth, links and contacts (2026-11-25, KB-SOFT-LOOPSTRETCH1, `soft-kernel/src/rigid.rs`).
- **The solve.** A woven sheet's threads, a triangle mesh's edges, rigid edges, the links of particles to bodies and the
  contacts of particles and faces with bodies are one system with the bodies as six-degree-of-freedom unknowns. It is
  solved by Newton steps, each a bounded conjugate gradient (MPRGP, Dostal and Schoberl 2005, with two-sided bounds:
  a row with no room is never freed, and a proportioning step stops at the far bound), and each taken as far as an
  Armijo line search allows, until every row is within its tolerance (0.1 percent strain for a sheet's threads, 1e-5 m
  otherwise).
- **Threads.** Fabric threads are compliant rows with their KES-F stiffness (XPBD's alpha over h^2), held rigid past
  EMT.
- **Friction.** Friction is a second, box-bounded solve (Kaufman et al. 2008).
- **Damping.** Rows with no compliance are damped by a share of their diagonal: sqrt(f32 eps) for contacts, the
  violation squared up to that for edges and links (Levenberg-Marquardt; Yamashita and Fukushima 2001). Without it,
  redundant rows (a flat mesh's edges, a light body pinched by a sheet) ran their multipliers off and rounding turned
  them into motion.
- **Evidence:**
  - `soft-kernel/tests/threads.rs`: a sheet stays within 0.1 percent at one to one and a thousand to one at any setting,
    and a damped step lands on the undamped step's bits.
  - `tests/soft.test.js`: a 1,000 kg box rests on a default cloth; the 1 g pebble's hop is derived from the sheet's
    ringing; a cotton strip sags as an elastic cable within 1 percent; a linked cloth keeps its momentum, woven or a
    mesh without shape matching; a pinched box leaves no faster than the sides close.
  - `tests/sail.test.js`: sailcloth-weight sails stay whole, with the load implicit.
- **Cost:** 4 to 42 times the sweep's (`docs/limits.md`).
- **Missing:** a quiet-machine measure of that cost, and contacts with another soft body's surface collider, which stay
  in the passes.

Soft contacts at no distance (2026-11-25, KB-SOFT-CUTTHRASH1, `kernel/src/probe.rs`, `kernel/src/face.rs`). A particle or
a soft triangle that touches an oriented mesh at no distance has no offset to take a normal from. It now takes the
surface's angle-weighted pseudonormal at the triangle, edge or corner it is on (Baerentzen and Aanaes 2005), walking the
fan of a corner through the triangles across its edges. Before, a particle took the reverse of its move, and a triangle
the manifold's arbitrary axis, so the two halves of a cut body pushed each other along and into each other.
- **Evidence:** `kernel/tests/face_sides.rs` (cut face on cut face, a face along an edge, a face at a corner, and
  particles at each, each failing without the change), and `tests/soft-cells.test.js` (the cut cube, every step within
  a derived bound and never under the box's top).
- **Missing:** an unoriented (two-sided) mesh still has no side to give at no distance.

## Couplings: gears, racks and pulleys in the kernel's substeps (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-24)

A gear, a rack and pinion, a pulley, a distance range and a path are rows of the rigid kernel's solve, in `packages/physics/kernel/src/couplings.rs`: a class of rows that grows with the world like the joints' (so a snapshot carries it), one row each (a speed that must stay zero: angular speeds along two axes at a ratio, a pinion's turn against a rack's slide, or the rate the two rope lengths of a pulley change), warm started at the start of each substep, solved in every pass beside the joint pass, with the error of a gear and a rack followed from the row's own speed substep by substep and a pulley's read from the poses, and a one-sided rope. Before this the three were per-step impulses in TypeScript, which left a nearly balanced Atwood machine (10:9) out by about g dt squared in its fall (3 mm at 60 Hz). Evidence: `kernel/tests/couplings.rs` (a gear holds its ratio rigid and soft, a rack moves a radius a radian, the pulley falls within one percent of the closed form at 3:1, 1.5:1 and 10:9, a slack rope does nothing, a replay gives the same bits) and `packages/physics/tests/mechanisms.test.js`. Missing: speed (build phase), none of the three is open: a coupling joins the islands of its two bodies as a joint does (`kernel/tests/couplings.rs` a resting train of gears sleeps as one and a touch on one end wakes it all; a spinning pair stays awake), and the table grows (a thousand gears in a train fit). A path's points live in the world's own growable column (`PATH_WORD`, a range of words for each path: its points, a box for each span and a box for each block of 16 spans, in the first body's frame, so the index stands still while the bodies move): a path that outgrows its range moves to a larger one at the end, a full column packs the live ranges together first and then grows, and the nearest-point search starts from the span the follower was last on and visits only the boxes nearer than the best found (`kernel/tests/couplings.rs` a bead goes round a closed loop of a thousand points sampling 4 spans a search, and paths grown together and removed keep their points).

Couplings against joints and float rounding (2026-11-28, `kernel/src/couplings.rs` `Locks`, `read_error`, `integrate.rs` `run_substeps`, `joints.rs` `solved_locks`, tests `kernel/tests/coupling_exact.rs`). Two changes to the kernel's maths. (1) Every coupling row is solved on the Schur complement of the locks of the joints the step solves on its moving bodies (at most 12 lock rows): it gives k - x^T K^-1 x, with x its cross terms on the locks and K their J M^-1 J^T inverted by Gauss-Jordan with complete pivoting (Higham 1990, a dependent row dropped), and reads the speed the locks will leave it, Cdot - x^T K^-1 (the locks' speeds); the couplings now go before the joints in each pass (a coordinates row still after them, as it reads the joints' own coordinates), so the joints' exact path solve takes back the rest of the push. A subset of the locks only frees the bodies, so it bounds the give from above and the row pushes short, never over. This is the treatment a joint's own limit already had, and block elimination as in R. Featherstone, "Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms", Springer 2008 (chapter 7, articulated-body inertia) and D. Baraff, "Linear-Time Dynamics using Lagrange Multipliers", SIGGRAPH 1996. Before it, a path holding a point 1 m off a slid follower's centre (inertia 0.01) kept a hundredth of each push and ran away (KB-PHYS-PATHMOVINGBASE1); now it holds 5.7e-7 m over 10 turns, and a cam follower sits at the closed-form lag a h^2 / (2 c) of a velocity row with a Baumgarte share c (J. Baumgarte, "Stabilization of constraints and integrals of motion in dynamical systems", Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 1, 1972) over 50 turns: 1.716e-5 m against 1.713e-5 at c 0.2, 3.49e-6 against 3.427e-6 at c 1. (2) A gear's and a rack's error is read from the poses after every substep, each body's twist about its axis since the row began (G. Dobrowolski, "Swing-twist decomposition in Clifford algebra", arXiv:1506.05481, 2015; in doubles, with an arc tangent good to 1e-14) counted past one turn, and a rack's travel; before, it was the sum of the row's speed and drifted by the f32 rounding of the poses, 2.7 cm in 100 turns of a rack (KB-PHYS-COUPLINGDRIFT1). Now the rack is 3.7e-6 m from the exact travel at z 0, 0.5 and 5 m and 9.8e-6 m at 50 m (one to two float spacings at the far end), and a 3:1 gear holds 4.1e-7 rad over 100 turns at 1, 50 and 500 m. E. Catto, "Modeling and Solving Constraints", GDC 2009, reads a gear's error from its joints' coordinates the same way. Missing: a coordinates coupling (`coupleDofs`) still sums its speed (KB-PHYS-COORDSDRIFT1, open); the Schur complement is formed for each row in each pass (12 by 12 at most), whose cost on many couplings is unmeasured (build phase); runs are native and Node on one machine.

Pairs of a removed body (2026-11-28, `kernel/src/events.rs` `pair_retired`, `wake_pair`, test `kernel/tests/retired_pair.rs`). `remove_body` takes each collider's body name at once and leaves its pairs for the next step's broad phase to drop, so between the removal and that step a neighbour's pair list holds pairs that name no body on one side. Every walk of a collider's pairs outside the step (`touch_collider`, `wake_touching_pairs`, `end_touches_as`, `set_body_enabled`) passes such a pair by: the live body wakes, the pair keeps its contacts and joins no list. Before, they woke row NONE, an access violation natively and a write to the word before the body column in Wasm (KB-PHYS-RETIREDPAIR1). Evidence: the two tests of `retired_pair.rs` end in STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION without the change. Still missing: a browser run of the same calls through the JS API, and a fuzz of API calls between steps.

The solver's own switches (`world_set_solver` 12 to 18, in the header so a snapshot carries them): friction solved in the pushing passes or only in the relaxing ones, the number of relaxing passes (a count set by the world is every island's), the friction model (a Coulomb cone at each point, or `simplified_friction` in `solver.rs`: one constraint at the manifold's mean point and a twist about the normal whose impulse is carried in `PAIR_TWIST`), the sweep's time floor, tolerance and advance count (`ccd.rs`), and quarantine (`check_range` takes a body out, QUARANTINED with DISABLED, in place of setting `lost`). `World::detect` is the collision-only step: broad phase, narrow phase and events, nothing integrated. `World::timing` holds 15 slots: the step, its seven phases, and the solver's `assembly`, `resolution`, `update` and `writeback` and the sweep's `ccdBroad`, `ccdToi` and `ccdSolver`, which are sums over the substeps or the bodies and stay out of the arena. Evidence: `kernel/tests/world_parameters.rs` (a block holds below tan t = mu and slides at g cos t (tan t - mu) under each friction setting; eight boxes stand under six combinations; a spun box stops in the time of its patch's twist under both models; the sweep stops by its tolerance, floor and advance count; quarantine against the stop), `tests/world-parameters.test.js` and `tests/detect-collisions.test.js`. Missing: speed of the simplified model against the Coulomb rows (build phase).

## ASCII post effect (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-24)

`packages/post/src/ascii.ts` is an LDR PostStack stage in two fragment passes: a (2 x columns) by rows rgba8unorm target holding each cell's mean colour and character index, then the full-size draw from an r8unorm glyph atlas made on the CPU at the cell size (rebuilt only when the ramp, cell or font changes, and after a device restore). `text()` copies that target and maps it. Evidence: `packages/post/test/ascii.test.js` (uniforms, atlas bytes, rebuild and release, readback and abort, bounds) and `ascii-browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (Intel Arc 140V: 405 of 405 characters equal the CPU reading, edge directions, bit-exact passthrough, resize). The same change makes `ScreenEffect.draw` keep a bind group when a caller passes a new `{ buffer }` object for the same buffer range: before, every screen effect made one bind group per draw per frame. Missing: no GPU time measurement.

## Sky and cloud depth in a live capture

Sky fog and the volumetric cloud march use the active scene capture's depth by default. Terrain, masked canopies and
other depth-writing surfaces stop the sky effects at their current silhouettes. A separately registered depth prepass
can omit meshes, so an explicit depth callback still selects that pass. At 4x the sky reads the current multisampled
depth attachment before it resolves. When the selected depth is unavailable, clouds use the empty-sky depth test and
fog has no surface to shade.

The proofs are the turning camera in `packages/sky/test/fog-motion-check.html` and the foreground pillar and block
inside the layer in `packages/sky/test/volumetric-check.html`. These compare automatic depth with an explicit live
capture and check the explicit unavailable-source behavior. The optical sources are Schneider and Vos (2015) and
Hillaire (2016), linked from the sky README.

### Fixed world-space terrain rings

Camera-driven clipmap snaps can replace ridge triangles without appreciable camera motion. Bounded `Terrain` and
`BiomeView` now keep a fixed world XZ anchor. `BiomeView` uses it for both terrain and horizon, while `TerrainStream`
selects a moving window on the fixed world lattice as tiles arrive. Both colour and shadow passes use the same ring
plan. A fixed anchor preserves static terrain shadows across camera moves. A rebase still updates local coordinates.
The terrain GPU regression in `packages/terrain/test/clipmap-anchor.browser.mjs` crosses a ring boundary with a
two-millimetre camera move. The legacy moving window changed 1,315 colour pixels beyond 16 code values and 786
silhouette pixels. Anchored terrain changed zero by either measure on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer.

### Water over coarse terrain rings

A clipmap ring takes the heights at its vertices only, so far off it bridges a channel narrower than its cells and the
depth test hides the water in it (KB-BIOMES-RIVERSTEP1). `@margoengine/water/banks` moves each water vertex toward the
eye along its own view ray until it stands as high as the rings' error there (slope times twice the ring spacing less a
texel, capped), which keeps the pixel and only lowers the depth, and drops fragments over the terrain heightmap at or
above the surface, so the waterline comes from the heightmap. Evidence: `packages/water/test/banks.browser.mjs` on
WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer (a 6 m channel's centre column: 153 of 400 rows before, 400 of 400 after, no
water past its walls). Missing: ground occluders within the allowed error in front of the water (a bank lip seen at a
grazing angle from a coarse ring) no longer hide it; the error is capped at 2 m and zero where the rings sample every
texel.

### Distant forest contact

The Terrain prepare pass can rasterize its drawn triangles from above before Scatter reads their height. The image
uses the original heightmap UVs and is rebuilt when the ring plan or elevation data changes. With a source peak of
154 m between coarse vertices, `packages/terrain/test/surface-height.browser.mjs` reads 104 m at that point on
WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer. Biomes' distant trees use that image, the placement graph and the chosen canopy kind.
Regional and tile queries return curvature in the same signed integer units before conversion to inverse metres.
The worker cover regression proves the distant mask matches the main-thread mask and loads the existing graph part
only when a canopy request supplies a graph.

### Scene sections with lighting providers

The Machinery section pass reserves mesh-shader binding 232 before the shadow and lighting passes run. Those
passes can read the same section planes for clipped shadows. Choosing a slot from the current entry count allowed
the shadow sampler and the clustered-light frame to share binding 4. WGSL requires distinct group and binding
pairs for distinct resources. The real-adapter `packages/machinery/test/section-open-check.mjs` proof attaches
both providers and verifies that the closed solid is capped and the open sheet stays open. The binding rules are in the
[W3C WGSL resource interface](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#resource-interface) and
[W3C WebGPU pipeline layout](https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#pipeline-layout).

### Section 5 evidence for heightfield relief lighting (terrain/relief-lighting, 2026-11-23)

An optional compute pass records the directional horizon and projected sky visibility separately so landforms
retain both broad cast shadows and diffuse shading. The fields are indexed by world XZ, independent of the
camera and of the surface color. The terrain clipmap evaluates both through one bilinear lookup in its lit pass.
The package also exposes the same bake and lookup for a caller's terrain mesh. Core and stage are outside this path.

The GPU regression uses an untextured ridge to verify east and west sunlight, open-sky versus valley irradiance,
zenith visibility, map edges and rebaking. The clipmap render in the same test verifies that the baked terms
change untextured pixels and that disposing the effect removes the render attachment.
[GPU regression](../../packages/terrain/test/relief-lighting.browser.mjs)

## Rough diffuse lobe (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-25)

`KHR_materials_diffuse_roughness` compiles `eonWgsl` (`packages/gltf/src/shader.ts`) only into extended shaders of materials whose factor is above 0. It is the EON BRDF of Portsmouth, Kutz and Hill (JCGT 14(1), 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18026): Fujii's Oren-Nayar single scatter plus a reciprocal multiple-scatter term, so the directional albedo of a white surface is 1. Evidence: `packages/gltf/test/diffuse-roughness.test.js` runs the shipped WGSL functions on the CPU against an oracle with the exact albedo (values, reciprocity, white furnace, albedo as the integral of the lobe); `packages/gltf/scripts/test-diffuse-roughness-browser.mjs` repeats the values on a GPU and compares pictures under sun, hemisphere and image-based light on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer.

## Display transform on a premultiplied canvas (section 5 supplement, 2026-11-25, KB-POST-ALPHARIM1)

On a canvas `TransparentCanvas` marks premultiplied, a display transform must take straight colour: `toDisplay(c / a) * a`
for 0 < a < 1 (Porter and Duff 1984), or silhouettes gain a light rim of about 36/255. Tonemap compiles its own variant
(`premultipliedShader`); every post effect that writes the canvas from a linear capture builds its display pipeline
through `displayFor(engine, code)` (`packages/shared/display.js`) and keys the pipeline on the mark, so an opaque canvas
keeps its shaders byte for byte. Evidence: `packages/post/test/alpha-rim-browser.mjs` (12 effects, WebGPU and the WebGL2
layer), `packages/headless/tests/transparent-gpu.mjs` (Tonemap chains, Node). Missing: DOF and water's screen composites
still encode premultiplied colour (opaque-canvas only for now).

SSAO's normal reconstruction (`extractShader`, KB-SSAO-SILHOUETTE1, same date): a background neighbour (depth 0) is not
a surface, so a silhouette pixel takes the depth step to its covered side and a one-pixel tip faces the camera.
Evidence: `packages/post/test/ssao-silhouette-browser.mjs` (SSAO and GTAO, 12 turns, both backends, no occluded pixel
on a lone face; 4 pixels down to 0.78 on WebGPU and down to 0.72 on the WebGL2 layer before).

### Section 5 evidence: conduction and phase change (FIRE-06, 2026-11-25)

The optional thermal entry loads a Rust Wasm SIMD kernel into the world's linear memory. Its cell-centred finite-volume method gives paired interior fluxes and keeps material coefficients with state for snapshot and restore. Both builds link in module slot 2 and allocate each instance's stack through the host. Sentinel tests verify that both builds leave the live arena intact, and the plain and shared worlds produce bit-identical conduction results.

`packages/physics/tests/coupling/thermal.test.js` compares diffusion to a slab's Fourier mode, tests conservation and the layered-wall equilibrium, and checks melting and freezing against the Stefan front. A grey-face test checks the combined conductive, radiative and convective energy balance against a prescribed surface temperature. The kiln regression establishes the temperature gradient and heat loss after exposing a hot surface to a cooler fluid. Coupling tests cover source accumulation, arena growth, frame-rate independence and bit-identical replay.

The backward Euler path shares the stencil and tests the exact discrete eigenmode at a stiff step, an enthalpy plateau during melt and freeze, and a grey face balanced at the new temperature. It also passes the replay and frame-rate tests.

The production thermoelastic solver reads the same temperature port in the PhysicsWorld. Its tests verify affine free expansion, the axial stress and support reactions of a restrained bar, stress continuity in bonded materials, and hydrostatic stress under full restraint. Frame-rate and snapshot tests exercise the heat-to-stress path. A failed equilibrium keeps the preceding published output. Browser checks verify that importing the optional entry leaves its Wasm unloaded and that the browser fetches the module when a solver loads, on both rendering backends.

In `packages/post/test/heat-haze-browser.mjs`, a changing thermal field displaces 2,123 native WebGPU and 2,131 WebGL2 compatibility fixture pixels by more than four RGB levels. The ambient, disabled, outside-volume and foreground cases each displace zero. The physics coupling tests verify a cooling gradient in photopic ceramic emission and the density decrease and expansion of heated gas at fixed pressure. The gas fixture supplies the pressure and mass balance while the flow and combustion solvers remain separate.

Remaining evidence includes scalability for stiff heat grids with the shared sparse kernel and new renders of the original kiln and turbofan shots.

### Surface energy and soil water (ATMO-09)

The weather entry uses a world-clock `SurfaceEnergySolver` for one patch or a rectangular batch.
The optional Rust kernel evaluates pairs of independent heat brackets and publishes deterministic
per-participant work. Prepared forcing and all prognostic arrays remain staged until every row solves.
The original scalar and optional native paths preserve the same heat and water budgets and the same
signed-cell snapshots. Tests cover forcing at the end of the clock interval and atomic rollback.
The RITS-10 fixture drives accepted surface wetness into actual materials from a moving rain band,
covering saturation, runoff and drying on both renderers. The original rainfall-runoff and flood
integration remains open.

### Section 5 evidence for two-mode plant motion (BIO-01)

The world arena holds the plant matrices, loads, two transverse modes and staged publication. Its plain and shared
vegetation modules use slot 3 and give each instance a stack in the arena. Velocity,
density and optional fluid inertia come from the same pure `FlowField` at the dyadic clock. The Wasm build proves
that instantiation does not modify an existing arena. `packages/physics/tests/coupling/vegetation.test.js` checks
uniform beam frequencies, midpoint phase and energy, delayed wind arrivals, depth-dependent water motion,
impulse and failure state, identical plain and shared results, and bit-identical replay.
`packages/scatter/test/states.browser.mjs` checks that the
crown shifts and the root stays in place in regular and tiled instancing on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.
The coupling suite also sends a rigid impact into a fixed trunk proxy, releases a preallocated fragment, and
restores a snapshot from before impact. The standing and released enabled states, pose and hash replay exactly.

### Catchment runoff and resolved flood inflow (HYDRO-02)

The runoff entry uses Rust SIMD for grid forcing and a topologically ordered finite-volume step for soil and surface
water. Green-Ampt integration solves through ponding. The depth–discharge relation is implicit and the ordered upstream
solve transfers the same water volume between adjacent cells. Depth, soil water, recharge and outlet discharge have
separate world-registry fields. The outlet field feeds shallow-water source terms on the simulation clock. Biome river
rendering accepts live discharge and historic flood classification can sample depth and velocity from the same flood
solver. The coupling tests close both volume budgets, reproduce the steady rating and ponding solution, verify the
response to rain and melt, and compare frame rates, snapshots and both Wasm memory modes. The renderer test changes the
inflow after attaching the view and observes the additional water volume on its real WebGPU river grid.

## Aquatic locomotion evidence (LIFE-03)

The optional swimming SIMD kernel reserves world memory slot 5 in plain and shared builds. It imports only
the world memory. Its region buffers contain state, commands and published fields. The loader gives each
solver instance its own stack. Unchanged slots and dynamic memory are checked at build time.

`packages/physics/tests/coupling/swim.test.js` verifies the exact thrust and drag reference models,
a physical bank, a centreline with conserved transverse mass centroid, pectoral station-keeping, hydrostatic
ballast and a breach. It exercises the actual SEA-02 surface, actual LIFE-04 intent and kinematics, and
identical replay across frame rates, snapshots and plain/shared memory. The BB-7 regression feeds the live
wake into `TracerSolver` and checks threshold, mass, current advection, settling and replay. The
`packages/environment/tests/swim-sediment.browser.mjs` fixture uses the active tracer mass for local
extinction on both graphics backends. The tail-wake render and articulated contacts still need integration.

Runoff stages the next seven grid planes and six cumulative ledger words before native acceptance.
The native soil and graph solves reject invalid numeric candidates. The timed rain and receiving
shallow-water regression routes the accepted outlet into Water on WebGPU and WebGL2 and checks
exact state and image replay.
Shared Wasm workers split independent cell work and join before the ordered water receipts
and drainage graph. The receipt data is runtime-only. Replay reconstructs it by running the same grid visits.

### Section 5 evidence for light-bodies aerodynamics (AERO-05)

The falling-body Wasm module integrates fixed-axis plates, fixed-axis blade strips and rounded grains in
world-owned memory. The two kernel builds are layout-equivalent in slot 7 and use only arena state, local
scratch and pinned math. The coupling suite checks closed-form trajectories and torque, APW motion regimes,
mirrored winged-seed rotation, arbitrary fixed colliders, frame-rate independence, plain/shared equality and
snapshots. Weather's PA-32 check follows measured hail speeds for two diameters. Its WebGPU fixture checks
position-driven changes and pixel-identical replay of the physics source. The camera-centred render path also
passes its existing hail assertions.

### Sediment transport and changing riverbeds (HYDRO-03)

The Rust SIMD sediment module consumes the shallow-water depth and discharge field. It conserves suspended and
bedload mass with shared finite-volume face transfers. TerrainBed receives Exner elevation changes on the
triangulated vertex areas, and the shallow-water solver samples the new bed. The mobile bed reserve limits erosion.
Registry fields expose concentration, bedload capacity and shear. A row-major concentration upload drives the
existing Flood tint on both rendering backends. Tests verify exact settling, bedload rating, a closed-form Rouse
profile, travelling sediment, bank migration with root stabilisation, boundary exports and deterministic replay.

## Pedestrian contact evidence (LIFE-05)

The crowd Wasm imports only world memory in either variant. Static data uses slot 10 and mutable
control, integration, neighbor and stack storage belongs to the world. A real NavMesh supplies
route points and grades. Node fixtures check the spatial gradient against an analytic head-on
encounter, the normal and tangential contact impulses against closed forms, equal and opposite
loads for unequal masses, rotational clearance, wall loads, queue release, input ports and
replay across frame rates and memory variants. The NavMesh regressions check weight in the
existing ORCA planner and preserve covered-target and wall guidance behavior.

### Boundary-layer wind on the world clock (ATMO-01)

The optional Physics boundary-layer entry uses the same pinned surface-layer profile as the scalar
Weather source. Workers sample disjoint grid rows and publish only after all rows complete. Arbitrary
time Wind queries run the same Wasm with a separate one-row scratch descriptor. Native tests cover
bit-exact far-cell replay and actual SIMD and turbulence work. AirSolver samples the wind at real
collider panels. The fixed-camera rain-shaft reproduction draws the coupled precipitation on WebGPU
and WebGL2. Held-out MOSAiC wind profiles and their misses are recorded in the Weather diagnostic.

### Live sediment and channel-bank evidence (HYDRO-03)

Sediment updates one accepted TerrainBed with shared vertex mass accounting. Its native SIMD workers prepare
individual cells and face proposals, with ordered bed transfer after joining. `sediment-threads.test.js` and
`sediment-threads.browser.mjs` verify exact parallel state, far-cell replay and work counts. The Water shallow
surface uploads accepted suspended concentration through its existing sediment tint. `sediment-surface.browser.mjs`
checks moving bed, water and same-state tint on WebGPU and WebGL2. The held-out capacity comparisons still miss.

### Native orbital evidence (SPACE-01)

The optional orbit entry compacts positive-mass sources in row order. Native workers partition target
acceleration updates, then join before the ordered J2 correction and symplectic kicks. The accepted
state is byte-identical across plain memory and shared workers. `orbit-threads.test.js` and
`orbit-threads.browser.mjs` cover far-cell shifts, snapshot replay, singular-state rollback and
actual work. WebGPU and WebGL2 draw the live accepted triangular solution in
`orbit-surface.browser.mjs`. Independently measured lunar ranging still exposes residuals.

### Underwater acoustic evidence (SOUND-03)

The optional Rust/Wasm SIMD tracer updates the same Gaussian beam and Snell arc state as the TypeScript
constructor. Each native worker writes its own candidate rows and exact counters. The host accepts the
step only after every partition and the published ports pass. `underwater-threads.test.js` and
`underwater-threads.browser.mjs` prove exact state across worker counts and far-cell shifts. The
fixed-camera `underwater-surface.browser.mjs` proves ray segments and pressure and delay labels on
both renderers. The measured arrival comparison remains open across the tank and ocean regimes.
Limits and source references are in the Physics README and the SOUND-03 audit.

### Geological landscape evidence (HYDRO-04)

The optional landscape kernel uses the world clock and occupies native module slot 12 in plain and shared memory.
It reads the canonical terrain height and held forcing ports, routes catchment discharge through a downhill graph,
solves the linear-slope stream-power equation downstream first and transfers grain volumes between vertices and
outlets. The same triangle areas define bed change, rain capture, and the sediment and uplift ledger. Optional
HYDRO-03 shear and root pressure alter mechanical thresholds. The bed applies each change on the following tick.

The fixtures compare the numerical step against the closed-form incision and pair-diffusion solutions, measure
sediment sorting and conservation, replay both memory modes, and read the updated heightfield of a live rigid collider.
The biome adapter samples the same bed triangles when preparing a geological snapshot for terrain rendering.

## Utility post passes (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-25)

`KawaseBlur`, `LUT1D`, `ColorAverage` and `DepthDownsample` are optional post entries; core and stage unchanged. All four
use fragment passes only, so the WebGL2 layer runs the same shaders. KawaseBlur keeps its pyramid in the effect's own
targets, one index range per view, and clamps the first pass to the view's rectangle, so split screens do not bleed.
Evidence: `packages/post/test/utility-passes-browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer
(blur spread and monotone edge, split-screen isolation, pixel-exact formulas for ColorAverage and LUT1D within one level,
DepthDownsample texels and normals equal to a CPU reduction in all four modes for 2 x 2 and uneven footprints), and
`utility-passes.test.js`. Missing: GPU timings, and a visual comparison of the blur against a large Gaussian.

## Render graph (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

`RenderGraph` (`@margoengine/post/render-graph`) is an optional post entry built on core's frame graph: two passes,
a capture at order -65 (the same SceneTarget capture and linear shader swap a PostStack uses) and the tasks at order
30; core and stage unchanged. Build: validation with coded errors, Kahn's topological order, transient textures
assigned to physical slots by lifetime. Evidence: `packages/post/test/render-graph-browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the
WebGL2 layer (scene then blit equals a PostStack HDR capture within 2/255, clear and copy reach the screen, a history
feedback loop accumulates 0.25 a frame, a Pixelate effect task), and `render-graph.test.js` (order, aliasing to 2
textures for 3, steady frames allocate nothing, resize, every error code, history swap once a frame, effect tasks
attach and detach on rebuild). Missing: GPU timings, the visual editor.

## Trail texture (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

`TrailTexture` (`@margoengine/post/trail`) is an optional post entry; core and stage unchanged. One frame-graph pass
before main, once a frame (marked in `onPreUpdate`, so multi-view frames update it once): a full-screen fade into a
second `rgba16float` target, instanced stamp quads with a fixed-function blend (screen, add or max), then a copy back,
so the exposed texture keeps its identity. Fragment and vertex work only, so the WebGL2 layer runs the same shaders.
Evidence: `packages/post/test/trail-browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (an unbroken line from a fast move,
black off the stroke, screen and add of two half stamps, 0.95^60 kept after one second, black after five) and
`trail.test.js` (stamp spacing, speed weight, smoothing, one update a frame, steady frames allocate nothing, the stamp
cap, validation, device restore). Missing: GPU timings.

## Mesh blending (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

`MeshBlend` (`@margoengine/post/mesh-blend`) is an optional post entry; core and stage unchanged. A frame-graph pass at
order 20 (after the main pass, before the stack composes) redraws the core meshes at 1x into an `rgba16float` tag
target and its own `depth32float`, reading each mesh's radius from an `r32float` table by entity id. In the stack's HDR
chain a key pass resolves each pixel to sky, untagged or a tagged key against the stack's resolved depth, then the
blend pass searches a golden-angle spiral, bisects to the seam, tests that both sides' slope-carried depths meet and
mixes in the mirrored colour. Fragment work only, so the WebGL2 layer runs the same shaders. Evidence:
`packages/post/test/mesh-blend-browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (a tagged box's seam with the ground
softens into red-green mixes; an untagged box's seam, the sky, the tagged box's pixels next to the sky and its sides in
front of far ground keep every pixel; untagging restores the frame) and `mesh-blend.test.js` (falloff, depth-slope
rejection from either side, options and tags). gltf/pbr models, materials meshes and terrain are tagged through the
capture hook SceneTargets uses (one hook per tagged model writing its radius and a key counted down from the top of the
key range), drawn into the same tag target inside the tag pass: `packages/post/test/mesh-blend-models-browser.mjs` on
WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (a tagged Box.glb sunk in a flat terrain softens its seam, the sky keeps every pixel,
untagging restores the frame, and tagging the terrain softens the same seam). Missing: GPU timings.

## Image filter graph (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

`@margoengine/post/filter-graph` is an optional post entry that runs on a bare `GPUDevice`; core and stage unchanged.
A graph compiles (`filter-graph-plan.ts`, no GPU calls) into full-screen passes. Fusion rule: a block joins its only
reader's pass when the read is at the reader's pixel or one unfiltered texel and both have one size; each block becomes
a WGSL function of `uv`, its names prefixed per node. Compilers inline these calls, so a producer is called from one
place (its colour kept in a `let` that the disabled branch reads too), and a chain fuses at most one texel read, whose
disabled branch needs a second call: calling twice doubled the code per fused block, and the first build, with an
11-block chain, did not compile within 150 s on the WebGL2 layer's Direct3D 11 route. Fused results go through `quantizeToF16` (clamped to the binary16
range), the rounding of the `rgba16float` intermediate they stand in for: without it an 11-block chain ending in a
chroma key differed by 5 codes of 255 from one pass a block; with it, none on the checked adapter. Pass uniforms are
one `array<vec4f>`; layouts are explicit; every fragment finds `uv` from `position.xy`, so merged and unmerged blocks
run at the same coordinates. All texture reads are `textureSampleLevel` or `textureLoad`, valid in any control flow,
so the WebGL2 layer runs the same WGSL. Evidence: `packages/post/test/filter-graph-browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the
WebGL2 layer (every built-in block draws; merged against unmerged within 1 code on six graphs: pointwise 11 passes to
1, texel 4 to 1, tree 6 to 1, steps 4 to 1, sampled 4 to 3, scaled and disabled 6 to 5; live values with no new
pipeline; canvas, texture, URL, stream and camera inputs; restore) and `filter-graph.test.js` (merge rules,
validation, no GPU object made in a steady frame, owners freed, loss). Missing: GPU timings, a run on a second GPU
vendor, and a physical camera.

## Optional SIMD wake transforms (SEA-04)

The CPU wake can load a Rust WebAssembly SIMD plan through `WakeSolver.load()`.
The plan copies the current input and output across its private memory on each FFT.
The world retains height, potential and velocity in its own arena. Bit-exact scalar/native tests
cover six mixed-radix grids, shared buffers and live wake replay. The existing Water agreement
fixture consumes the native wake on both renderer backends.

## Contact sound evidence (SOUND-04)

The optional Physics modal kernel converts per-track mechanical excitation to audio-rate sample ranges.
The contact adapter owns the rigid kernel step and publishes contact loads. A separate solver reads
the contact and fracture fields and owns the acoustic state, on the world clock. Native plain and
shared kernels import the same arena layout and keep no evolving state in static memory. CPU regressions
cover the analytic impulse and held-force convolution, resting contact, rolling versus sliding,
rupture, 44.1 kHz allocation at 120 Hz, frame-rate independence and replay. The Physics README uses
an actual browser audio destination to verify the rendered signal.

The landscape stages its new material, ledger and bed delta before publishing. It checks that the
accepted delta can be represented in the receiving float32 TerrainBed. Biomes copies the accepted
terrain into the relief that drives the fixed-camera Terrain test. The volume check includes the
last contribution still pending on the staggered terrain step.
Shared workers prepare disjoint vertices and downhill links before the deterministic drainage graph.
The existing Biomes helper opts into shared memory when its caller asks for multiple landscape threads.

### Drainage fog evidence (ATMO-08)

`DrainageFog` uses the PhysicsWorld arena and pinned thermodynamics. Its coupled tests verify heat and water through
phase change, Stokes deposition, downhill forcing from `TerrainBed`, real `SurfaceEnergySolver` exchange, open-edge
export, conservative fog transfer and shared/plain replay. The environment medium exposes the same optical layer to
the froxel pass. Its browser fixture moves the resolved patch on WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility and verifies that
removing the medium restores the clear frame. This covers the fog portion of PA-34.

### Snowpack evidence (ICE-01)

`Snowpack` keeps mass, enthalpy, geometry and cover in its PhysicsWorld arena. Each Wasm variant has an empty
data section and tests verify that loading leaves a filled arena unchanged. `snowpack.test.js` checks phase
energy, compaction, wet retention, exact conduction, cornices, live slope stability and frame/seek replay.
It reads the actual surface-energy entry and feeds the shallow-water/runoff entries through the registry. The browser test
renders the snow before and after melt through Weather's existing surface path on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.
The existing avalanche now reads the live pack at release. Its tests check mass conservation at a building
face and reduced momentum through a vegetation patch. The powder-cloud model uses its separate transport.

### Aeolian transport evidence (EARTH-07)

`AeolianTransport` owns its arenas and writes conservative change through `TerrainBed`'s accumulation field.
The native module imports the selected world memory and has an empty data section. The native-load regression
checks every byte of a populated arena before and after each instance. `aeolian.test.js` checks the backward-Euler
reaction, a Pomeroy–Gray snow equilibrium including cover, mass through open and closed edges, repose and world
snapshot determinism with both memory variants. `blown-sand-check.mjs` renders an exposed ridge on native WebGPU
and on the WebGL2 compatibility layer. ATMO-01 and ATMO-06 registry readers are covered by coupling fixtures until
those solvers accept the physical fields. TREE-5 still needs a filmed-scene integration.

The native phases now batch slope, forcing, local source exchange and diagnostic work. Each helper has its
own stack and disjoint vertex partitions. The caller joins each phase and routes faces, hops and avalanches
in one order. Coded input and native status failures leave the accepted arrays and ports untouched.
`aeolian-workers.test.js` tests exact 1/2/4 participant replay with signed origins and paired work counts.
`aeolian-workers.browser.mjs` starts actual isolated Chromium helpers from the bundled package assets.
The ridge test uses accepted snow transport to drive production BlownSand and checks exact playback on
each renderer. ATMO-06 receives mineral dust on its compatible grid. ATMO-01 stress feedback remains open.

### Groundwater evidence (HYDRO-06)

The optional Rust SIMD groundwater kernel imports world memory in both modes. It has an empty static data
segment and only an instance-local stack pointer. Its build instantiates over a sentinel and checks every byte,
including the existing rigid-kernel window. Aquifer controls, storage, forcing, ports and iterative work use
world-owned regions. Snapshot hashing includes the controls, storage and ledger.

The groundwater check verifies the fixed-head Dupuit profile, spring activation within an implicit step, wetting,
the world clock and both native memory modes. HYDRO-02 supplies the exact water leaving its soil, and HYDRO-01
receives the actual seepage volume. The aquifer and the surface solver keep independent volume ledgers.
The production browser bundle fetches both kernels under cross-origin isolation and reproduces the same state
hash in the two memory modes.

### Grounded glacier flow and drainage (ICE-02)

`@margoengine/physics/glacier` imports world memory and runs its own SIMD Wasm at level 0. Face-wise
volume conservation, a positive donor limiter and the sparse implicit solve are checked on analytic
and stiff non-flat grids. Layout-1 f64 fields expose thickness, crevasse depth, velocity, drainage
and per-step releases. Real HYDRO-01 matches discharged melt volume. Identical full hashes cover
plain/shared Wasm, frame-rate changes and snapshot replay. The wave-source fixture verifies only
delivery of released volume to a registry reader. A SEA-06 impulse response needs its own solver.

### Ground locomotion kernel (LIFE-02)

The optional `@margoengine/physics/locomotion` Rust crate prepares gait geometry and applies grounded forces in
two narrow exports per body. Both memory variants import the world's memory, use static slot 13 and lease an
arena stack. Only profile construction and Bed sampling are in TypeScript. Linear contact work is measured by
the configured number of links or feet plus torso, and each one gets its own sampled load.

The Physics fixtures verify inextensible link closure, analytical slip force, a passive spring load, stance and
swing wrenches, the live TerrainBed interface, deterministic replay after a snapshot, and the two memory variants
after growth. The focused browser gate checks lazy loading, contact-driven motion and snapshot restoration.

### Iceberg capsize and conservative wave sources (ICE-03)

The no-static-data native module imports the world arena and uses a world-allocated stack. Its
planar face integrals give the pressure and moment before every kick. The registry path carries
real ICE-02 calving volume into the body queue and paired SI volume patches into the existing
WakeSolver. The coupled test checks crest and trough, zero mean water gain, freshwater mass
balance, replay and equal hashes using distinct plain and shared memory.

### Forest crown competition kernel (BIO-03)

The optional `@margoengine/biomes/forest` builds its crown-neighbour table in world-assigned scratch each
ecological year. It rejects separated crowns using squared distances and computes exact integer overlap depths
in two SIMD lanes for each remaining pair. Its Rust Wasm has no initial data and imports the world memory in both plain and shared variants.
The build instantiates each variant over sentinel-filled memory and verifies every byte is intact. An independent
offline integer reference checks annual births, mortality, snag cleanup and living crowns. World tests exercise
the surface-water and landscape ports, exact exposure replay, and a retained growth axis after the wind drops.

### Grounded biped and quadruped gait kernel (LIFE-01)

The optional legged entry extends the slot-13 SIMD ground kernel with configurable phase and speed, body load and
contact surface velocity. The stance controller allocates each active foot its share of a bounded force and couple.
Controlled gait profiles live in extra state, preserving the existing uncontrolled ground-animal snapshot layout.
The optional deck adapter reads the real rigid `bodies` port and returns the opposite integrated `bodyImpulses` per
substep. The direct HorseMotion path shares the same support concepts and stays renderable without a PhysicsWorld.
Verified with real terrain, a moving rigid support, plain/shared memory and browser replay.

### Pack ice as a separate world solver (ICE-04)

The optional Rust SIMD module leaves the shared module address area untouched. Its floes and all
work regions belong to their world. The field bridge uses the existing rigid body layout and
impulse accumulator, including when SEA-08 applies buoyancy to the same body. The contact
regression compares those opposite impulses and the Water regression checks the matrix boundary.
The coupling harness establishes one hash across frame cadence, both memory modes and snapshot
restore. Continuous-sheet blocks and grounding are outside the current planar pack model.

### Civil impact work and rigid coupling (BREAK-03)

`CrushSolver` reads the versioned `bodies` port and accumulates linear and angular impulses at the same point for both bodies. The published deformation and work ledger, contact latch, and pending impulse rows survive snapshot restore. Closed-form spring, perfectly plastic, hardening, and compacted backing references check energy and stroke. Two-body and fixed-barrier runs check momentum, offset torque, transverse misses, and persistent seal loss. A floating service craft uses the same rigid row for live seakeeping and a quay impact. A released seal or shell seam can open the matching SEA-10 compartment.

`crushInertiaChannel` pairs a layout-1 hull mobility field with a crush impulse receipt.
For each matching dynamic hull the mobility row stores a presence marker and the
two world-frame matrices `(M + A)^-1` and `M (M + A)^-1` about the rigid centre of mass.
The staggered schedule publishes mobility before the crush step and applies its mapped
impulse in the same rigid tick. The hull reads that receipt on the following step so
the ordinary external-load estimate excludes work the contact already resolved.
Five focused tests cover live carried and exterior water inertia, cross-axis response,
Coulomb sticking, and schedule and replay behaviour. The channel is local to the
optional solvers.


The optional shell contact manifold applies separate normal and tangential forces at verified
local distance minima of each rigid sphere against the live sheet. It assigns one owner to
each shared mesh feature. Native tests cover folded and flat sheets, opposing normal loads
with continuing friction, and exact plain and shared replay. The folded sheet is rendered
on WebGPU and WebGL2. Arbitrary rigid shapes and shell self-contact remain open.

For fixed hulls, SEA-10 returns a layout-1 pressure row per linked shell seam.
The shell consumes the prior flooding row and the hull consumes the current
deformed opening. The native shell integrates the resulting pressure along
the current face normals. The support-reaction and vented/unvented fixtures
verify the feedback and catch reversed tick order. Dynamic rigid attachments
and fully coupled fluid stress are still open.

The shell's opt-in work record stores the native interval's force-pass counts.
The test at 32 and 128 faces uses identical element size and substeps, and
checks linear membrane and hinge work and exact shared-memory replay.
[Work-count recipe](../whitepaper/reproduce.md#break-03-native-shell-work)

Staged crush envelopes extend the same contact path with trigger peaks followed by
folding at lower loads. Their increasing permanent offsets separate return work from
elastic recoil. The continuous contact uses the rigid rate and rejects an active
unresolved negative tangent with a rate remedy. The full-scale 34.1 mph rail coach
test uses a published pretest design input and holds out the measured gross
displacement and velocity during compression. Rebound remains underpredicted.


### Thin films on rigid panes and open ground (FLUID-07)

The thin-film module imports world memory and reserves no static data. Film and input buffers are
transactional during a step. The solver consumes the live rigid body record and authored plane,
turns physical precipitation into intercepted water, and sends independently held impact pressure to
the optional WakeSolver. Depth, capillary redistribution, drying and edge drainage have independent
closed-form or volume checks. Plain/shared builds, frame cadence and restore agree bit for bit.
For a strip with one row or column, the pressure operator has five bands. The hysteresis
augmentation adds a cell diagonal and keeps that band structure. Each substep uses a free
pressure solve to initialize the wet-area rate and reuses one augmented Cholesky factor across
the constrained iterations. A three-mode regression covers 20 μm cells in either axis under
both Wasm memory modes.

The planar conjugate-gradient solve takes the principal factor of each face line when mobility
varies appreciably across the patch. The line factors borrow the consumed transport workspace
for the duration of the pressure solve. Each matrix application keeps the cross-line gradient
and curvature terms. At stronger stiffness it reduces the residual correction to the
stiffness-weighted cell operator, then rechecks the complete face equation after reconstructing the
flux. Hysteresis over-relaxes the split update and measures convergence on its actual residuals.
Water-cap, viscous-cap and rectangular Neumann regressions cover the three pressure choices.

### Environmental airborne batch (ATMO-06)

The optional native kernel integrates two Cartesian lanes at once, with a third scalar lane in the same operation
order. Host-side queries supply each particle's local Wind conditions, then the solver runs the batch over its
arena state. Both native module initializations leave sentinel-filled world memory untouched. Direct checks cover
the closed-form Stokes trajectory, exact droplet mass changes, source buffering and two real producers through
the field registry. A production Vite build preserves both lazy Wasm files.

### Developmental plant growth (BIO-02)

The Biomes entry reads current HYDRO-02 water through the registered soil storage field and publishes versioned branch geometry. The phase, stable parent graph, radii and in-season water sums survive snapshot restore. The SIMD shadow kernel allocates its own arena stack and has no static window. Geometry conversion uses the existing Procedural tube entry. Tests derive the apical and lateral allocation, branch angle, attenuation, and radius from the production law, then exercise drought, solid occlusion, plant competition and wasm/browser replay.

### SEA-11 native strip tables and live deck sources

The optional Wagner bake packs independent angle evaluations in Rust Wasm and gives deterministic ranges
of hull stations to native workers. A live HullSolver admits tables only for its body-frame mesh, density
and station count. Deck inlet records use the same receiving cell as the shallow-water calculation and
the full accepted deck surface can be copied between world steps. The Water technical proof draws that
surface and checks exact accepted-state replay on both renderers. Measured loads beyond the early wedge
model, load on hatch structures, and the original film cuts remain open.

### SEA-08 guarded hull publication and native panel workers

HullSolver bounds live sea samples and the force columns. Its transaction restores any force, wake,
deck, flood and memory writes of a failed step. In each long radiation and diffraction ring it saves
the writes for the current tick. Independent panel systems run on optional private Wasm workers and join
in reference-frequency order, with f64x2 row updates. Fixed-camera Water tests draw the accepted hull and
displacement wake on both renderers. The original lake footage and large-amplitude regimes remain open.

### SEA-14 native water-entry section profiles

The optional Physics entry profiler loads Rust Wasm with one participant by default, or uses the native worker
pool to process disjoint cut-plane ranges. Within each plane the signed fan sum keeps the original triangle order.
Only the accepted forces, cavity, splash events and wake sources reach the world. The regular constructor reads
the same closed mesh with TypeScript. Invalid sampled pressure and non-representable force roll back the candidate.
The Water tank proof draws the accepted events through ShotSplash on WebGPU and WebGL2 and checks full frame
and world-snapshot replay. Measured slam timing, resolved curtain, surface seal and original film cuts remain open.

### SEA-13 accepted surface foam

The foam solver stages coverage, breaker records and the clock before publishing the accepted fields. A Rust
module advances disjoint grid lines in each direction with f64x2 coverage and decay-weight updates. The
caller joins the lines between sweeps and saturation. 39 × 31 and 71 × 37 scalar and threaded checkpoints
remain byte exact after signed relocation. An optional Water surface effect reads the accepted coverage
without accumulating it in Water’s own history. The fixed-camera cutaway checks both renderer backends.

### Native outdoor path integration (SOUND-01)

One solver tick samples the actual Wind and TerrainBed in their signed cells. The optional native module
uses private Wasm memory for the staged atmosphere and terrain paths. Workers integrate disjoint links.
Each SIMD lane keeps deterministic per-band order. The two legs of a blocked path keep separate time and
distance accumulators. Path records publish together after all inputs and results pass their finite-range
checks. Spot checks cover 35 and 63 links at 1, 2 and 4 participants, exact shared and plain world replay,
and a 50 m OfflineAudioContext and fixed-camera bell cutaway on WebGPU and WebGL2.

### Native room pressure kernel (SOUND-02)

Two-lane Wasm updates the seven-point pressure stencil. The world owns both pressure buffers, the receiver
trace and its sample counter, so alternating buffers and the published trace survive snapshot restoration.
Both modules have no static data. Instantiation over sentinel-filled shared or plain arena memory must
leave all existing bytes intact. Scoped tests check rigid standing modes, wall dissipation, exact arrival
around a doorway, sample-timed excitation and browser packaging of both lazy kernels.

The native job partitions padded stencil pairs on optional shared memory. A joined boundary before
each source and receiver update preserves alternating-buffer order. Coded numeric failures preserve
both accepted pressure arrays, the sample clock and trace. Focused Node and bundled browser tests
compare exact replay with one, two and four participants and a signed origin. The concert-hall
cutaway uses the same paths for visual cues and its convolved audio on both renderers.

### Viscoplastic material points (FLUID-06)

The isolated SIMD module has no static writes on instantiation. The world hashes the live
material rows, reference-volume ledger and published fields. The 27-node APIC transfer,
local plastic return and optional occupied-node PCG step run in arena memory. The coupling
fixture joins a registered inlet to a real TerrainBed and checks the exact mass ledger and
matching restore. It compares both memory modes at actual shared and plain instantiation.

The viscoplastic solver rejects nonrepresentable pressure, volume and solvent reductions before
publishing. It stages the accepted inlet and outlet budget with the candidate and caps explicit
work at 4,096 microsteps per tick. Its particle adapter compacts active records into the existing
screen-space liquid passes. A timed flume regression checks the accepted motion and HDR replay
on both WebGPU and WebGL2.

Optional shared workers own disjoint slices of the active-node list and material slots.
A barrier separates normalization, the ordered solvent solve, contact and material return.
The ordered scatter and per-particle escape fold preserve the serial rounding path.
Worker receipts and stack memory are outside the physical snapshot.

### Isothermal gas in the existing soft kernel (SOFT-06)

The optional soft kernel adds an isothermal pressure constraint to its closed-surface pass. The rest of the soft step
and its staggered rigid coupling use the same solver. Gas packing, external pressure and constraint mode are native
snapshot columns. Closed-form affine-volume tests cover both signs of the pressure difference and vacuum. The
world fixture shows actual rigid contact, matching hashes across frame rates and restoration of both gas controls.

### Physical road driving (DYN-04)

RoadDriver reads registered body poses and ATMO-09 relative wetness and writes its controls on the 60 Hz world clock. The binding carries tyre spin and transmission state in the solver's arena. The banked display mesh is reused for collision and wheel contact. Dimensional checks cover friction-limited curves, deck momentum, pressure-sinkage, a wheel crossing a lip, physical curved-route tracking and weather loads on a massive procedural vehicle. The film fixtures record the contact and motion evidence separately from the original shot reports.

### Natural long waves and moving shorelines (SEA-06)

The optional native solver reads the live TerrainBed or aligned vertical displacement and
one or more 60 Hz natural SeaSource producers. It imports arena memory, checks that its
module initializer leaves the arena untouched and keeps its registered records stable
across snapshot restore. The independent cases cover the Ritter fan, rest,
small-amplitude travel, the wet-patch bottom filter, and a real glacier-to-iceberg bay pulse.

### Thin-disk transport and exterior relativistic trajectories (SPACE-03)

The accretion entry has feature-local plain and shared Rust SIMD builds. The positive tridiagonal solve uses one row
per annulus and exports density, heat flux and orbital phase through the registry. Both memory modes leave the arena
intact when instantiated. The Kerr tracer uses pinned elementary functions, signed radial and polar velocities and an
exterior log radius. Tests cover steady heating, stiff mass balance, circular rates, radial and polar turns, infall,
frame dragging, a null orbit and exact replay.

### Thermo-viscoplastic lava transport (EARTH-10)

The optional `@margoengine/physics/lava` entry joins the 60 Hz solver graph. A slot-free Rust SIMD module imports world memory and uses solver-owned grid, state and variable work regions, with a private stack in the arena. The mobile layer uses an HLL flux with hydrostatic reconstruction against terrain plus stationary crust. A symmetric stencil transfers enthalpy between occupied cells. Surface skin balance, basal cooling and an implicit Bingham friction update supply the thermal and momentum source terms. Native code subcycles to the transport and diffusion limits. State is published only after the owned candidate passes those checks.

`TerrainBed` supplies a heightfield. ICE-05 returns absorbed heat, liquid and steam through the existing layout-1 fields. SEA-06 consumes the layout-1 displacement rows. The tests cover direct analysis, live bidirectional thermal transfer, a downstream wave, render-frame cadence, snapshot replay and the two browser memory variants. The producer also publishes solid deposit elevation for the next granular terrain consumer.
The native terminal path evaluates a viscous face law, with a factored depth derivative and donor
drainage limit. Physics publishes only after checking every solver surface, heat and source receipt.
Weather draws the accepted column skin and crust directly. Fixed-camera GPU tests compare the
timed early surface, advanced front, cooled crust and exact replay on both renderers.

Shared lava workers partition the stability calculation, independent face sweeps and per-cell source
and cooling updates. They join between sweeps and fold ledgers in grid order. Exact Node and Chromium
replay, worker counts on two large grids, and rejection of late publication cover this path.

### Native free-surface preview water (FLUID-02)

The optional PBF module uses a SIMD kernel in an imported PhysicsWorld arena without static slots or startup
writes. The caller-owned sparse grid probes 27 cells in a fixed order and reports candidate work. Solver state
is the reserved point rows, statistics and in-flight rigid impulses. The grid and boundary poses rebuild from
that state and the existing body field. Deterministic playback is checked across plain and shared memories.
The renderer draws the same solved points on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility backend. The current evidence
includes a published surge timing comparison, a real offset rigid impulse and a native replay.
Artificial pressure uses the solver substep squared relative to 60 Hz. The kernel preserves rest for
free-water pairs outside the active density constraints, checked separately from the surge data.

### GPU particle liquid (FLUID-02 and FLUID-03, parity bar P13)

`GPULiquid` in `@margoengine/water/liquid` is the real-time liquid: MLS-MPM in five WebGPU compute passes a substep (six with surface tension, whose pass takes the gradient of the
density on the grid for the continuum surface force the grid update applies), at
most five storage buffers a stage (particles, grid, collider sums, mesh distance fields, the live count, plus the
uniform), no readback in the step. Emitters write their particles in one dispatch after the live count, and drains
are removed once a frame by a stable prefix-sum compaction (block counts, one workgroup's scan, a ranked scatter, the
new count) and one buffer copy. Colliders are signed distances in the WGSL: sphere, box, capsule and plane in closed form, a
mesh as a trilinear field (`bakeLiquidMesh`) with its normal by central differences; the collider sums are read and
cleared in one submit, and `link` hands linked bodies those impulses on the CPU, one frame late. GPU
maths: every particle-to-grid and collider sum is an integer `atomicAdd` of a fixed-point term (2^16, impulses 2^10), so
the result does not depend on the order of the adds and a run repeats bit for bit on one GPU and driver; the grid
update writes the node's f32 velocity bits over its integer sums in place. The WebGL2 backend has no compute, so the CPU
twin runs the same passes and uploads the particles for the same surface draw. Evidence: the CPU twin's closed-form
and conservation tests and the GPU-against-twin check on WebGPU and `--compat`
(`packages/water/test/gpu-liquid-check.mjs`, Intel Arc 140V). Missing: a speed comparison with the three.js compute
fluid (speed phase) and a run on a second GPU vendor.

### Rail wheelsets and catenary (DYN-05)

The optional rail solver owns layout-1 f64 car and cable regions. It consumes ATMO-09 wetness directly through the field registry. The numeric state includes springs, axle speeds, controls and wire deflections. The Rust SIMD cable kernel works in the same arena and has no active static data in either memory mode. Its two lanes carry lateral and vertical waves. Focused proofs cover static axle loads, rolling distance, cant, a rail joint, wet-braking slip, coupler reactions, wire lift, contact loss, deterministic scrub and rendered asset motion on both backends.

The surveyed curve acceleration is even in travel direction. `rail.test.js` proves the sign and
magnitude for both curve hands, signed-origin port replay, and atomic rejection of derived overflow.
The private native catenary job partitions velocity and position passes with a join at each boundary.
The force assembly remains ordered. `rail-wire-workers.test.js` covers the discrete two-axis mode and
exact 1/2/4-participant replay. The packaged browser test starts three actual catenary helpers.
`rail.browser.mjs` checks the outward roll and exact same-frame replay during both wet-curved passes.

### Terrain-contact footprints (EARTH-05)

An optional slot-free SIMD kernel rasterizes pressure-driven indentation and redistributes loose volume using
TerrainBed's exact triangulated nodal areas. The native state keeps the maximum indentation, while the area-integrated
ledger splits cut material among the berm, compaction, dry fines and outflow. The optional rigid adapter observes the
existing wheel and belt loads and refits the registered height field. The adapter snapshots the belt shear history and
the collider-height mirror. LIFE-01 foot rows are another input. ATMO-06 consumes the same mineral dust grid used for
aeolian sources. Tests include both clocks at their shared times and audit the held source mass at an intermediate tick.

Both tiers use the same coupling contracts. The resolved tier balances integrated vertex pressure with the input
force and exposes a layout-1 pressure grid. The native repose sweep transfers unconstrained, newly deposited loose
soil across each grid face at most once per step. It schedules only faces adjacent to current loose material
and visits them in the same order as a complete sweep. A transfer schedules any later faces it can reach.
Reported work gives raster-vertex visits and candidate faces examined, and the volume moved is auditable without a timer.
The browser fixture rebuilds the Terrain mesh from the published bed sampler on demand. The same physical relief
reaches WebGPU and WebGL2 without transferring a solver-specific render texture.
The optional hardpan uses a continuous two-regime bearing curve. The resolved native kernel brackets its
force integral, accounting for stations that reach the layer and those that still load homogeneous soil.
The rolling option integrates normal and shear stresses on the loaded arc. Its moving projected footprint
uses the published rigid load and signed shear displacement, and the bed continues to feed the collider.
The configured hardpan depth and excavation bedrock can use separate vertex grids. Their copied values are
snapshot state. Soil cuts reference the same floor data supplied to TerrainBed, so no rejected volume enters
the compaction, berm or dust ledger.
The optional wheel-phase field carries one angle per external row. The native rolling profile combines
the steady rim bearing envelope with the live projected lug tips before normalizing the bed pressure.
An indexed tread can extend beyond the rim. The native kernel intersects its rotated triangles with
the local bearing plane and takes the lowest triangle at each occupied profile sample. Geometry lives
in snapshot regions. The profile is temporary arena storage rebuilt each step.
The camber field supplies the actual right-axis vertical component from the rigid step.
The indexed mesh combines that tilt with its spin before intersection. It still shares the
same force-normalized bearing footprint.
The opt-in wheel reaction port adds one snapshot record per external row. The native kernel
integrates net drawbar and axle torque once after finding the loaded arc. The root finder still
integrates only the vertical force required for its bracket. Unloaded rows are cleared before export.
In a staggered rigid–soil–bed group, the rigid wheel consumes the previous reaction on the same
collider. The chassis receives a tangential impulse and the wheel's separate spin state receives
the axle impulse. A coupled work bound uses the current point velocity, enabled axes and inertia.
Tyre state, reaction samples and the paired terrain state all participate in seek.
Opt-in skid holds free-rolling exit and peak angles while the native bracket balances the
two signed shear regions. An optional shear radius derives the slip from relative wheel and bed
speeds down to zero travel. The same rigid impulse bound handles the reversed axle moment.
The optional right-axis force field pairs the combined rim shear with the sidewall pressure
integral. The rigid adapter applies it after longitudinal traction, then recomputes the current
