contact velocity. The lateral impulse respects the available grip and stops at zero side slip.
The optional cross-track depositor reweights the actual loose cut volume into separate
repose-slope banks. It enumerates only their projected node bounds, schedules their faces
for the same conservative repose sweep and records the share of each missing bank as export.
Grouser transport takes its volume from the same cut ledger. It uses the rear area's current
excavation capacity and sends it to the opposite bank when the projected corners align.

The dry granular resistive-force solver reads TerrainBed and the rigid body pose and velocity
on the world clock. Each SIMD lane integrates a separate submerged strip sample from the
published anisotropic stress law. The native reduction preserves sample order. Forces and
centre-of-mass moments accumulate through the existing rigid field and survive snapshot restore.
The calibration plate stresses and measured rotating-leg force traces come from separate experiments.
The optional cyclic bearing model stores the highest pressure, corresponding compliance and previous
elastic displacement per bed vertex. A compact active list unwinds only the prior reversible cut.
The new contact subtracts its elastic height and accounts for permanent soil displacement separately
in the shared bed and mineral flux. The active list and history are snapshot regions.

### Divergence-free particle pressure

The optional Physics liquid entry owns no static native data. Plain and shared SIMD kernels use the
solver-owned regions for particle state, warm multipliers, sparse buckets and viscosity work. The coupling
suite checks rigid linear and angular reaction, clock and restore identity, and pressure-driven modal PCM.
An isolated Water fixture draws the same simulated particle state on WebGPU and WebGL2. The emitted world
fields have executable consumers. A real HYDRO-01 wet-cell test verifies same-tick mass and horizontal
momentum, refusal and replay, with vertical momentum in a separate receipt ledger. The physics queue
records the required owner's reservation and applied-flux receipt for wet/dry cells and breaking crests.
The native capillary energy has a flat-interface normalization derived from its cubic kernel.
A measured 34 g droplet oscillates in 0.885 s against the 0.742 s Rayleigh prediction.
The DFSPH pressure step includes rigid recoil in its Jacobian line solve through the existing bodies port.
At a 1,000:1 liquid-to-rigid mass ratio the real plate and particle reach the closed-form shared velocity
in one iteration, with matched impulse, nonincreasing kinetic energy and exact replay on both memory modes.
A separate off-centre direct-contact check uses the same mobility in a local normal and tangent solve.
It verifies reciprocal force and torque, zero inward speed, the selected tangent damping and kinetic energy loss.
The implicit viscosity system includes reciprocal body impulse and world-axis motion. The isolated
light-plate case now reduces joint kinetic energy from 8.789 to 8.780 J, matching its analytical exchange.
The optional impact field records the work of real hard-contact impulses, their energy-weighted position
and arrival time, and the number of contacts for one clock tick. Reads of the record survive replay.

### Natural granular runout (EARTH-02)

The optional Rust SIMD kernel keeps depth, discharge and sampled bed in world-owned regions. It uses a separate trial region with no static arena writes, and updates the published field only when the complete Courant-controlled step succeeds. The coupling fixture keeps a closed mass ledger on a rectangular grid over a live triangulated ridge. Resting pressure balance, dry-front positivity, Voellmy drag, pressure-supported release, 24/30/60 fps cadence, snapshot parity and the isolated browser's plain/shared kernels are checked independently. The roughness tier anchors the low-speed transition to measured start/stop curves and uses the local plane metric for Froude. Rotated-axis equilibrium and the two held-out chute velocities use the same stored solver state. The deposit phase freezes qualifying cells into the TerrainBed accumulator after advection. It saves the receiving height contribution and the conserved mass with separate horizontal impulse and energy receipts. On the next step the solver reads the topology it changed. Its optional coastal port carries one signed volume per cell and saves the previous marine occupation. The source and terrain change participate in the same transactional publication. A combined underwater consolidation test resolves the net void created by densification, with bit-identical native browser replay. The optional seismic input reads the registered surface-acceleration records and interpolates each column before applying the deterministic friction projection. The live SeismicGround coupling replays its response across memory kinds.

### SEA-08 forward-course radiation history

`HullSolver` can add the ordinary-strip longitudinal speed terms to its existing heave and pitch loads on the rigid-body port. It stores relative heave velocity and dynamic pitch in the world arena. Analytic forced-response, constant-trim, stability-range, and plain/shared snapshot tests exercise the new path. Measured head-sea response, following-sea and roll response, and live cabin props and sea feedback still need separate evidence.

### SEA-08 to SEA-04 waterplane flux

An opted-in `HullSolver` writes signed waterplane volume at the same world rate as `WakeSolver` can read it. The producer ignores a fully submerged or dry hull. Its optional layout-1 source rows reside in the world arena and retain the public state on replay. One-way volume transport, pitch and roll dipoles, and propagation beyond the hull footprint have direct coupling cases.

### SEA-08 forward-speed viscous roll

`HullSolver` caches a bare hull's geometry-dependent forward roll coefficients from the same still-water stations as radiation. It uses the course's water-relative longitudinal speed in the lift, friction, and eddy terms before folding them through the existing angular impulse. The analytical torque comparison checks inferred speed and an explicit current-relative override. The production browser fixture checks the moving course hull and deformed wake on both backends.

### SEA-08 encounter-frequency incident forcing

The correction to heave and pitch is computed from the spectral components while the old strip convolution continues to read the live water field. Each distinct section form retains the frequency-domain heave mass and damping only when a forward course and spectral diffraction are in use. A tapered-hull beam-wave control isolates the mass gradient. Head and following waves check the signed encounter terms, and a live wake at depth checks that the correction does not replace the water signal.

## Points on a deforming mesh (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

`@margoengine/animation/deformed-points` adds no deformation arithmetic: it binds the deformation pass's output (`PBRPrimitive.deformed`, 80-byte vertices at `deformedOffset`) as an instance-step vertex buffer and draws a four-vertex strip per vertex in pass order 1, after the batched deformation pass (order -10). `Animation` skips a model whose nodes are all hidden unless a reader is counted for it (`packages/animation/src/deform-readers.ts`), which the points register while set up. Evidence that exists: the CPU test (size maths against direct projection, recorded draw, reader count) and the browser check on native WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer (every vertex's point on its projected pixel, hidden model, skin and morph). Evidence still missing: no run on a second GPU vendor or on Firefox and Safari, and no measured frame cost for large meshes.

## Morph weights per crowd member (section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

`@margoengine/animation/instanced-morph` keeps `SkinnedCrowd`'s vertex stage and adds one step before its `skinned` call: for each block of the vertex's primitive (one entry texel naming the first offset texel and the weight index), a non-zero weight adds the target's position and normal offsets, read with `textureLoad` from the bone texture after its bone rows. Weights live in the instance row as `array<vec4f, ceil(targets / 4)>`, so the crowd keeps VATCrowd's six bindings, its shadow caster and its lighting hooks unchanged; the text of the stage is `skinnedCrowdVertex` with four edits (a CPU test takes them out and compares). The order, morph then skin, is the deformation pass's. Evidence that exists: the CPU twin against the analytic strip and the baked offsets; the compute readback of the vertex stage against the twin and the pixel comparison with the model, on native WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer. Evidence still missing: no run on a second GPU vendor or on Firefox and Safari, no measured frame cost at the 64-target limit, and the upload is the whole instance buffer rather than the changed rows.

## Voxel path tracer viewport while the camera moves on the WebGL2 layer (KB-VPT-ROUTE-MOVING, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

On the layer the trace kernel is a route of fragment programs that the CPU drives, and a frame's batch of samples
lands in a later frame, once its last census is read back. A view therefore tells two restarts apart: one for the
camera alone keeps the image on screen and lets a batch that starts an image run on, and the batch is shown when it
lands as the image of the camera it was traced with (history reprojected into that camera, first-hit depth of that
camera); any other restart (scene, options, size, device, a released view) drops the batch and the image. A batch that
only adds samples to an image the camera has left is dropped, so the new camera's first batch starts sooner. Evidence
that exists: `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/route-moving.test.js` (a recording device: every frame of a moving
camera draws the image of the camera one frame before; the two kinds of restart) and the `denoisemoving` case of
`tests/browser-check.mjs` (RTX A6000, layer on ANGLE Direct3D 11: 4.38 denoised and 16.07 raw against the converged
image at the last position, 16.09 for one raw sample at rest; 186.28 before, when no traced image was drawn;
WebGPU 4.14 and 16.09). Still missing: the lag in frames measured in a page that draws at the display's rate (the
case's frames do not wait for the display), a run on ANGLE Metal and OpenGL, and a second GPU vendor.

## Synchronous raycasts on GPU-deformed meshes (KB-BVH-SYNCPOSE1, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

A skin or morph pose is written by a compute pass into a GPU buffer, and WebGPU has no synchronous readback, so a CPU query can test the drawn pose only if the same arithmetic runs on the CPU. Each deformer now registers that evaluation per primitive (`packages/shared/pose-source.js`): `Animation` runs the deformation shader's terms in `packages/animation/src/pose.ts` (morph deltas times weights, then the weighted sum of four or eight palette matrices, the cofactor normal with its handedness flip, a final normalize) on a palette computed as `upload` computes it, `inverse(node) * joint * inverseBind` in float32; `Skin` hands over the vertices its CPU `pose` already made; `GeometryCachePlayer` hands over the array it uploads. `@margoengine/bvh` reads every model primitive through `primitiveEntry`, which swaps in the posed vertices while `deformed` is set and refits one tree per pose (Wald, Boulos and Shirley 2007).

The two evaluations are not bit-equal by construction: the CPU sums in float64 and rounds once, the shader works in float32 and WGSL lets a compiler reassociate and fuse. Evidence that they agree: `packages/bvh/tests/gpu-build-browser.js` in `test:browser` (RTX A6000, D3D12, Chromium) reads the Fox's deformed buffer back at three times of its clip; every CPU position is within 1.00 float32 step of the largest coordinate of the GPU's (the check allows 4), every normal within 1e-4, and 102 synchronous first hits equal `intersectModel`'s on the read-back vertices. On the CPU, `packages/bvh/tests/deformed-sync.test.js` compares 900 rays with a brute-force scan and `packages/animation/tests/sync-pick.test.js` checks a skinned strip against its closed form.

Still missing: the same comparison on Metal and Vulkan drivers (a fused multiply-add there moves a position by a step, which the bound of 4 is meant to cover but no run has shown); eight-influence and morphed assets on a real GPU (their CPU arithmetic is tested against closed forms only); dual quaternion skins on a real asset rather than the twisted tube (`SkinningMode.blend` gives `Animation` their CPU pose since 2026-11-27: 9.5e-7 from the read-back GPU pose, scripts/animation-dqs-tests.js; a mode without `blend` still refuses with `unsupported`). `BatchedMesh` and the weights a `MorphWeightPlayer` samples on the GPU have one since 2026-11-27; the player's CPU samples match its read-back GPU weights within 1.9e-6 (scripts/animation-morph-gpu-tests.js, RTX A6000, WebGPU). The WebGL2 layer runs no deformation pass (`Animation` needs WebGPU), so there is nothing to compare there.

## Voxel path guiding on ANGLE Direct3D 11 (KB-VPT-GUIDE-D3D11, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

Evidence that now exists: `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/guiding-browser.mjs` runs its values on WebGPU, on the
WebGL2 layer on ANGLE Vulkan and, on Windows, on the layer on ANGLE Direct3D 11; the three give the same guided error
(10.24 against a baseline of 350.05). Before, the Direct3D 11 leg read 807,472: a loop left by `break` after a
`continue` picked a wrong box face there. The fault is ANGLE's translation (KB-LOOP-D3D11, next section), fixed in
the layer for every package.

## Loop headers and lone cases on ANGLE Direct3D 11 (KB-LOOP-D3D11, KB-SW2, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-26)

ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end (Chrome 157, RTX A6000) splits a loop header holding `?:`, `&&` or `||` into statements,
rewriting the loop as `for (; s; )` with its update and condition put before each `continue` in the body, including a
nested loop's: the translated HLSL of the guide's program (`WEBGL_debug_shaders`) shows `j++` at the face loop's
`continue`. It also drops no-op clauses from the end of a switch, and Direct3D 11's compiler then runs a lone remaining
case for every selector. The layer's GLSL (`packages/webgl2-compat/src/glsl/emit.ts`) writes such a loop with no header
when a loop inside it continues, and an empty default clause first; nothing else changes. Evidence:
`packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-control-flow-browser.mjs` (fifteen shapes, native WebGPU and the layer on ANGLE
Direct3D 11 and Vulkan against a CPU reference; twelve wrong on Direct3D 11 before, none after) and
`test/glsl.test.js`. The loop shape is in `glassCandidates` of the voxel path tracer and sciviz's AMR ray march. Missing:
Intel and AMD under Direct3D 11, and a corpus record of the guide's program.

## Lossless and 12-bit JPEG (lane C, 2026-11-26)

- One reader, `packages/shared/jpeg.js`, serves `decoders/jpeg`, `decoders/image`, `decoders/tiff` and the exporters:
  DCT files of 8 and 12 bits and lossless files of 2 to 16 bits (ITU-T T.81).
- Quality bar: lossless output is exact (libjpeg-turbo files for every selection value, and the NEMA DICOM references);
  lossy 12-bit output is within 1 level of libjpeg-turbo's floating point decode. `tests/jpeg-t81.test.js` pins both;
  `tests/jpeg-nema-corpus.mjs` is the by-hand run over the whole NEMA set.
- Evidence still missing: ITU-T T.83's compliance streams (sold with the standard), a DNG file from a real camera (the
  tile shapes are proved with files the test writes) and a TIFF with 12-bit or lossless JPEG from a third-party writer
  (the strips are libjpeg-turbo's, the TIFF container is the test's).
- Arithmetic, hierarchical and DNL-height files are refused with code `unsupported`.

## Ambient replay under blended coverage (section 5 supplement, 2026-11-27)

- SSAO and GTAO subtract `ambient * (1 - visibility)`, so the replayed ambient light of a pixel must never exceed what
  the picture holds. Anything blended over a captured surface without owning its depth draws an ambient veil
  (`packages/shared/ambient-veil.js`): its coverage, black, over the replay target. `Scatter`'s covered rings do.
- Evidence: `packages/scatter/test/grass-ao.browser.mjs` checks the bound `shut >= open * visibility` per pixel
  (12,231 pixels broke it before, 0 after, RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer);
  `packages/post/test/ssao-silhouette-browser.mjs` checks one-pixel slits (KB-SSAO-LONEPIXEL1).
- Covered depth (KB-SCATTER-AOFRINGE1): a covered blade writes depth where a hash of its coverage passes, so such a
  pixel's colour is mostly the surface under it. While an occlusion effect reads that surface (`wantUnder`), `Scatter`
  holds its covered depth back from its colour pass (order 1.5, `markCover`) to `<name>:cover-depth` (order 1.52).
  Pass order in such a frame: 1.5 scatter colour, 1.51 `ssao:under` (depth copy U, ambient replay and veils of the
  surface under the blades), 1.52 covered depth, 1.53 `ssao:covered` (depth copy Dc), 10 `ssao:extract` (centre depth
  C = U where Dc != U and the scene depth D == Dc, else D; late veils such as smoke over the under replay; the
  extractor and kernels place the pixel at C and search occluders in D; the ambient light where C != D is the under
  replay). A frame with no covered blade runs today's passes on today's bindings, bit for bit.
- Evidence: `packages/scatter/test/grass-ao-fringe.browser.mjs` (GTAO and SSAO, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer, RTX
  A6000): pale pixels 4,226 to 1,096 (GTAO), 2,038 to 155 (SSAO), the grass still darkening over 3 percent of the frame,
  and a view without blades byte-identical to one without grass and to the build before the change.
- Missing: veils for blended meshes and particles; SSGI and SSR composites under blended coverage are not measured;
  the pale pixels left are as frequent on blade-depth pixels as elsewhere (the pixel-scale variation of the hashed
  occluders), not yet bounded on a second GPU.

### Section 5 evidence: planet brightness input (2026-11-27)

`PlanetTerrain`'s `brightness` uses the spare fourth byte of the snorm8x4 normal, so the vertex stride stays 20 bytes.
Evidence: `packages/terrain/test/planet-recipes.browser.mjs` on WebGPU and webgl2-compat (RTX A6000): brightness 0 draws
the same bytes as none, rays only lighten, -1 draws black ground, no validation error. Missing: other hardware tiers.


## JPEG 2000 decoding (decoders/jpeg2000)

One clean-room Rust crate, `packages/decoders/jpeg2000-kernel`, builds the committed `src/jpeg2000.wasm`
(`node packages/decoders/scripts/build-native.mjs jpeg2000`; scalar Wasm, no SIMD until a work count or paired A/B
shows a gain). Only the optional `decoders/jpeg2000` entry and its worker load it, by
`new URL('./jpeg2000.wasm', import.meta.url)`; compute's ONNX ImageDecoder imports the entry when a model holds a JPEG
2000 stream. Each image gets a new instance of the compiled module, so Wasm memory is released with it and a trapped
instance is never reused. Core and stage are unchanged.

Quality evidence: `cargo test` in the crate (marker syntax, tag trees and packet headers, the five progressions, the
three coding passes against a test-side MQ encoder, both wavelets, JP2 boxes, the Wasm interface, size limits);
`packages/decoders/tests/jpeg2000.test.js` (Node, calling thread and workers) and
`packages/compute/tests/onnx-image.test.js`; OpenJPEG-written vectors, a browser worker run on both backends
(`decoders/tests/jpeg2000-browser.mjs`) and the fuzz run below. `decoders/image` routes the format. Conformance:
`decoders/tests/jpeg2000-conformance.mjs <folder>` runs the T.803 (11/2002) decoder tests from a hand-downloaded set
kept outside the repository (the crate's `t803` example for the 78 reference components, the shipped Wasm for the nine
JP2 files), all passing 2026-11-27. It is not part of CI, which has no copy of the set; rerun it after a crate or
`jpeg2000-codec.ts` change. A JP2 restricted ICC profile is converted on the host by `decoders/src/icc.ts`: the Wasm
returns 16-bit samples and where the profile lies. Missing: the sets of the 2021 and 2024 editions. Sources: Rec.
ITU-T T.800 and T.803; Taubman and Marcellin (Kluwer, 2002); Taubman (IEEE TIP 9(7), 2000,
<https://doi.org/10.1109/83.847830>).

Transparent canvas alpha in temporal and lens passes (2026-11-27, KB-ALPHA-TEMPORAL1): every filter on a premultiplied
canvas works on linear premultiplied RGBA and gives alpha the colour's weights (Porter and Duff 1984; Smith 1995). TAA
(`taa/src/alpha.ts`) patches the finished resolve, settle hash and present shader, keeps coverage in history alpha and
the reactive history in `historyDepth.g`. DOF (`dof/src/alpha.ts`) patches the gather, near-chain and join kernels after
the lens and half-resolution patches. SceneFade lerps with a blend constant. Pipelines follow the canvas mark of
`shared/straight-display.js`; opaque shaders are unchanged. Evidence (section 5): `taa/test/alpha-browser.mjs`,
`dof/tests/gpu/alpha-check.mjs`, `post/test/scene-fade-alpha-browser.mjs` and `alpha-rim-browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the
WebGL2 layer, RTX A6000, TAAUpscale included. Engine views (`post/test/alpha-views-browser.mjs`, both backends): TAA
and DOF in two views and SceneFade over overlapping views keep the alpha; it found variance clipping moving colour and
alpha apart, now clipped as one 4D point (KB-TAA-ALPHACLIP1; Salvi 2016; Karis 2014). Missing: XR on a transparent
canvas (water's composites followed, KB-WATER-ALPHARIM1).

TAA silhouettes (2026-11-27, KB-TAA-EDGE1): the default resolve takes the motion and expected depth of the nearest
surface in the 3x3 neighbourhood (closest-depth motion, Karis 2014; FSR2's dilation) and keeps history when that depth
lies inside the depth range of the 3x3 history footprint (TAAUpscale's test; Nehab et al. 2007), where it took each
pixel's own motion and tested each tap. Evidence (section 5): `taa/test/stability-browser.mjs`, a thin post round an
orbiting camera, edge alternation 3.26 to 0.179 sRGB levels fast and 2.92 to 0.225 slow on WebGPU (RTX A6000), bound
0.25, no trail behind a box crossing the wall on both backends. The WebGL2 layer at 4x read 2.89 and 0.335 until
KB-TAA-COMPATEDGE2 (0.175 and 0.231 since, asserted).

JPEG 2000 hostile input (2026-11-27, KB-J2K-HOSTILE1): headers can ask for far more memory and work than their bytes
carry, so the kernel bounds tile-components (2^20), structures per tile (2^22), packets by header bytes and visits by a
per-decode budget; coefficient arithmetic wraps. Evidence: `decoders/tests/jpeg2000-fuzz.test.js` drives the shipped
Wasm in a worker with a 10 s watch per case (structure-aware mutation of OpenJPEG streams; Manes et al., "The Art,
Science, and Engineering of Fuzzing", IEEE TSE 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.00140; Pham et al., "Smart Greybox
Fuzzing", IEEE TSE 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.09447). Missing: the ISO/IEC 15444-4 corpus, coverage-guided
fuzzing, and streams using code-block style options from an outside encoder.

Lightning glow (`@margoengine/sky/lightning-glow`, 2026-11-27): one fullscreen additive pass at order 6.54 that reads
the scene depth; each pixel integrates single scattering from up to 4 x 64 straight channel pieces (fragment storage
buffer, camera-relative, rows rewritten each frame). The shader mirrors `lightningGlowRadiance` line for line:
12 ray points by `t = t0 + h sinh(q)`, 6 channel angles split at the phase peak. Evidence:
`packages/sky/test/lightning-glow.test.js` and `features-check.mjs lightning-glow` (GPU against CPU, native WebGPU and
the WebGL2 layer, 4x and 1x, RTX A6000). Missing: other GPUs, timing, multiple scattering.

### ATMO-03 cloud projection and field-driven render path

Cloud convection can load a plain or shared Rust SIMD Neumann stencil outside the Physics root and World entries.
The cloud step computes a complete candidate state, traverses the pressure stencil in stable order and checks the
operator residual and corrected face divergence before committing. Origin cells and accepted mean wind follow
world snapshots. The Environment density-volume path converts accepted cell-centred liquid water to extinction
and uses the existing two-backend volume pass. The closed-cube check, native worker replay and fixed-frame browser
regressions cover these three paths. Independent cloud-field measurement and deep moist dynamics are open.

### ATMO-06 natural airborne parcels and spray density volumes

The optional parcel solver samples local Wind and staged sources into a per-tick candidate. Rust SIMD
integrates disjoint ranges through the existing world-worker helper. Receipts verify work before an ordered
contact and mass fold commits parcels, work and the registry fields. The accepted phase shares the same
snapshot layout across worker counts. The Environment layer maps accepted sea spray to local optical depth
on the existing volume pass. CPU tests verify candidate rejection and cross-section. The fixed-camera
browser fixture covers both renderers and the restoration of the same draw state.

### LIFE-03 swimming workers and the pectoral wake cutaway

The optional native swimmer applies the same diagonal updates to independent body rows, with X/Y SIMD.
A shared world can split ordinary and passive-reaction rows across workers. The caller checks replies before
committing all fields. World-cell metadata comes directly from the swimmer's host. A reciprocal passive-load
fixture verifies the shallow-water impulse and the BB-7 cutaway renders the accepted fin-to-sediment transfer
through the final settled bed on both renderers.

### BIO-01 signed field sampling and plant worker phases

Rooted plants translate station positions into the supplied air or water origin cell before sampling. The caller
computes the input differences at the world clock and gives each native worker a disjoint candidate interval.
Only complete, checked modal state is copied to the field backing. Placement, shape and displacement use the same
physical Scatter adapter in the fixed-camera sea-surge fixture. Signed origin, rejected calculation, worker replay,
frame-zero rigid activation and both renderers have scoped tests.

### ATMO-02 synthesis and gust evidence

The optional Weather turbulence entry retains pinned noise and tensor evaluation. Its asynchronous FFT transforms
each of the three complex fields twice with the Rust Stockham plan. A build can use one, two or three participants,
each with a private plan. The 512 × 32 × 32 test counts 3,145,728 transformed complex values and 179,306,496 SIMD
twiddle products. The published URL keeps Wasm and the worker script as separate assets. The production browser
test loads both from an application build, starts two helpers and checks the library build's external Wasm asset.
The solver and renderer test carries the placed gust through the signed wind cell to rooted clumps on both backends.
The independent Vindeby vertical co-coherence remains outside the model's seed spread.

### AERO-01 signed fields and native traction

WindForce samples collider-panel positions in the wind's signed origin. The rigid kernel gives fallback bounds
in the collider frame, including the surface centre's offset. The native backend partitions the implicit load
probes, with f64x2 traction and torque pairs and ordered reduction. The coupled proof covers 4,291 panels and
279 thousand panel calls in five steps. Both packaged assets and real helper startup are checked in Chromium.
The AirSolver and RigidSolver keep their existing world contracts. The paper mobile verifies the live load
through rope constraints and renderer poses on WebGPU and WebGL2.

### ATMO-08 accepted columns and fog optics

The published column and optical regions keep their layout. Internal candidates hold the dry and liquid-water
longwave closure, native work slots, updated mass ledger and optics. A finite CFL substep must advance the clock.
The workers resolve independent local columns, while donor-face transfers and the ledger follow canonical order.
A packaged worker test starts three helpers from a production application. The valley cutaway transfers real cold
condensate over TerrainBed into FogGrid, with identical state and same-frame RGBA after seeking on both backends.

## Terrain bump height near the camera (KB-TUNDRA-GROUNDNOISE1, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-28)

A height that feeds a screen derivative must not come through the hardware sampler where a texel covers several pixels:
the filter weights are rounded, a bilinear height has one slope a texel, and texel noise becomes slope. Terrain's `bump`
reads the layer's 128-texel mip with a cubic B-spline over exact texel loads below a footprint of 1/128 of a repeat.
Evidence: `packages/terrain/test/bump.browser.mjs` on an RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer; the shader variants
(tint, floating origin) by `packages/terrain/test/surface.test.js`. Missing: no run on a mobile or integrated GPU, and
no timing of the extra texel loads (build phase).

## A clear colour is a string or unset (KB-BIOMES-BLACKSKY1, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-28)

Both backends: core's WebGPU renderer and the WebGL2 preview renderer treat only undefined, null and false as no clear
colour; every other value reaches the colour check and throws a RangeError at the next render. Before, an `[r, g, b]`
background cleared to core's near-black colour with no error. Evidence: `tests/clear-capture.test.js` (attachment and
drawn clears, first and later views, the preview renderer); `packages/post/test/scene-background-browser.mjs` on WebGPU
and the WebGL2 layer (RTX A6000). Core + stage 25,149 B gzip before and after. Missing: other GPUs and browsers.


## Section 5 evidence: anatomy core and the human table (rigging overhaul group 1, 2026-11-28)

Rigging has a body model. `@margoengine/rigging/anatomy` fits a species table to any rig from landmarks (joint
positions and the facing), and `@margoengine/rigging/anatomy/human` holds the human table in ISO/IEC 19774 names.
Limits come from the table and are on by default; solvers, the validator, retargeting, the ragdoll and `addPerson`
read it in the groups that follow (the human rigging plan in the untracked private folder, groups 2 to 7).

Evidence that exists:
- `packages/rigging/tests/anatomy.test.js`: one body as a T pose, an A pose and arms down, with rolled bone axes,
  mirrored, and with elbows or knees modelled bent, bends every hinge the anatomical way and reads the same angles
  and skeleton for one posture (positions to 1e-9); every one of the 137 limited joints of the table round trips
  angles to pose to angles (1e-6 degrees) and turns about its own table axis; the stops hold (elbow and knee 5
  degrees past straight, KB-RIG-ARMS2); a bent knee keeps its bend under sideways noise; a straight knee does not
  twist; a hand's twist moves into the forearm with the hand unmoved (1e-12); a spine region's budget holds; the
  older projector fed `poseLimits` stops the same elbow at the same angle; the roll of a straight limb is recovered
  from motion to 1e-6 degrees.
- `packages/rigging/tests/anatomy-human.test.js`: the table is the 139 body joints of figure 4.13 with the level 1 to
  3 joints and parents of the standard; the meaning of every motion of every joint (407 checks); a second copy of
  every source number; the datasets against typed copies; the stop rule; the spine shares; the namings of Mixamo, the
  CMU BVH and ASF skeletons, 100STYLE, Character Creator, HAnim 1.x and 2.0, VRM humanoid and Roblox R15.
- `tests/anatomy-clips.test.js` with `tests/fixtures/anatomy-clips.json`: every motion capture in the repository
  played through the structural limits, with what they change recorded per clip.

Evidence still missing:
- No frames yet. The pose sheet (front, side and three-quarter views at each joint's range ends, on WebGPU and the
  WebGL2 layer) is built by group 2 and is where the table is judged against the anatomy references.
- No number is checked in print: 90 are from recall. The print sources are the AAOS 1965 booklet, the AMA Guides 5th
  edition, White and Panjabi 1990 and Kapandji.
- Nothing calls the limits yet: `addPerson`, the IK solvers, the retargeter and the ragdoll still run without them
  until groups 3, 5 and 7 land. No demo changes on screen from this group.
- The structural allowances are policy values with no measurement behind them.

## Composites outside post on a transparent canvas (KB-WATER-ALPHARIM1, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-28)

Water's liquid, underwater and caustics composites, post's SurfaceCaustics and weather's LensDrops encode straight colour
on a premultiplied canvas. Evidence: `packages/post/test/alpha-rim-browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (RTX
A6000); `packages/post/test/straight-display.test.js` scans every package for the pattern. `ParticleLiquid` and
`Underwater` also write the coverage their medium makes, so empty pixels they fill are not see-through
(KB-WATER-LIQUIDALPHA1): the same test's liquid and underwater cases. `LensDrops` writes the coverage of its glint
(KB-WEATHER-LENSGLINT1): the same test's lens case, which, like the others, reads coverage from a grey page because
added light clips on a white one. Missing: other GPUs and XR on a transparent canvas.


### AERO-03 native wing lattice

The optional flight entry loads one native lattice at a time per wing. Private Wasm memory holds panel geometry,
matrix rows and post-solve induced velocities. Each participant owns disjoint target rows during matrix and wake
phases. The caller pivots and eliminates in the scalar order. Both paths compute local moment arms before shifting
the wind sample to its signed field cell. Accepted work reports actual matrix, wake and elimination SIMD operations.
The 51- and 95-panel coupling cases reproduce scalar forces, circulation and rigid replay at 1, 2 and 4 participants.
A fixed-camera Aviary regression checks full-frame replay on both renderers. Dense wing storage is quadratic.
Rotor annuli, full aircraft wake feedback and the original flight timeline remain outside this proof.

## Source-size gate and WGSL redeclaration check (quality gates, section 5 evidence, 2026-11-28)

Two gates aimed at where fixes cluster, not at file size for its own sake. `npm run quality` gains `source-size`
(`scripts/quality/source-size.js`): no hand-written package source passes 100 KiB, and the 24 over it on 2026-11-28
(`scripts/quality/baselines/source-size.json`, soft.ts 358 KB down to probes.ts 103 KB) may grow 4 KiB each before
they must be split along a seam; generated Wasm blueprints and tables are left out. The shared CPU test harnesses now
reject a shader module that declares a module-scope WGSL name twice (`tests/support/wgsl-redeclared.js`), the class of
KB-WATER-RIPPLEDUP1, which twice reached main because only the GPU saw it. Evidence: `tests/quality-gate.test.js` (the
gate on a fixture tree) and `tests/wgsl-redeclared.test.js` (the water clash, every declaration kind, no false hits on
locals, members or comments); every test file reaching those harnesses ran with the check on. Missing: package tests
with their own mock device (about 340 files) do not call the check unless they import it, and the gate measures bytes,
not how many concerns a file holds.

### SEA-10 flood-table clipping and accepted compartment state

The optional Rust variant uses f64x2 pairs without changing the triangle or fan summation order of the TypeScript volume integrals. The shared variant partitions sample planes across the caller and up to three private workers. Scalar and native world snapshots match through signed-origin replay. Compartment reads copy accepted world state. A failed non-finite sea query restores the previous level table and keeps the last accepted flood result. The same WebGPU and WebGL2 fixed-camera fixture checks a hull that changes list, trim and draft because its tanks fill. Ruponen's independent basin curves still disagree. [Verification and limits](../limits.md#progressive-flooding-evidence-and-limits-sea-10)

### SEA-15 native parcel diffusion and accepted plume state

The optional native Wasm variants preserve each parcel's Philox key and counter and pinned Box–Muller output. A batch covers independent active rows and runs paired counter rounds with up to three native helpers. Ordered water, wind and bed samples remain on the caller. The accepted step journal retains occupied parcel rows and their ledgers. A late malformed field sample restores the tracer's accepted bytes. Node and packaged Chromium check exact state and signed-origin replay, and the cutaway checks the live release, deposit and renderer pixels. Measured static crater deficits remain outside the model's diagnostic intervals. [Bounds and evidence](../limits.md#accepted-parcels-and-independent-jet-scour-sea-15)

### FLUID-07 implicit face matrix and rolling-pane acceptance

The optional native matrix phase splits the same cell pressure and face operations over disjoint ranges. Global reductions keep their established order. The film validates candidate wave, water, load and detached-drop outputs before replacing accepted regions. A scoped late-overflow test checks all accepted bytes and exact retry. The directed rolling pane uses projected precipitation and sends detached drops into a second film. Two renderer paths replay its full resolved output and accepted snapshots from inside and outside. [Limits and evidence](../limits.md#accepted-film-motion-and-independent-incline-drops-fluid-07)

### BREAK-03 ordered shell face assembly and accepted contact

The optional crush entry partitions shell membrane and pressure faces across native workers. Each range writes a private result before the caller assembles face forces in canonical order. The 211-face shared fixture matches the preceding scalar Wasm and reports accepted work across four participants. The fixed-camera dock fender checks exact accepted snapshots and full renderer replay independently on WebGPU and WebGL2. Arbitrary-shape shell contact, automatic tearing and the original EF-11 shot remain open. [Evidence and commands](../whitepaper/reproduce.md#break-03-accepted-shell-and-civilian-fender)

### SEA-03 native wave pairs and surface-to-hull evidence

The nonlinear sea evaluates second-order pair terms in SIMD and reduces them in the original scalar sequence. Optional helpers own disjoint pair ranges, publish intermediate terms, and leave physical sums to the caller. The signed-cell, finite-depth crest matches the scalar normal exactly, including the spatial taper derivative. The accepted surface drives the same live launch that the dual-renderer fixed-camera cutaway shows. The proof leaves two-way feedback and phase-resolved focusing open. [Evidence and commands](../whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-03-second-order-waves-and-independent-flume-counts)

### SEA-01 accepted spectral transport and wave-field rendering

Spatial fluxes are independent across transverse lines and spectral bins. Optional native participants use the same scalar limiter and preserve the split sequence, returning finite candidates before the wave solver publishes its clock, friction and field. The WebGPU and WebGL2 cutaway draws the propagating spectrum after an upwind gust ends and checks the resulting buoy motion and exact replay. The physical source terms and angular refraction stay on the caller. [Evidence and commands](../whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-01-accepted-wave-transport-and-lake-george)

### SEA-05 accepted radiation stress and wet sand

The surf solver computes native directional moments in canonical order, then synchronizes before the divergence pass. Forcing, wave energy, roller and wet history publish together only after validation. The two-renderer cutaway reads the accepted shallow-water surface and wet-sand history. [Evidence and commands](../whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-05-accepted-surf-and-boers-flume-gauges)

### SEA-07 native head composition and accepted tide

The optional surge workers evaluate the rationalized Sun and Moon tide terms and the pressure head in separate phases, with the wet pressure and tide totals reduced in canonical cell order. The surge publishes only after both phases succeed. Scalar and native tests exercise the same accepted shallow-water and geocentric state at signed origins. [Evidence and commands](../whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-07-tide-replay-and-lake-superior)
